1"""Shared multi-tensor (foreach) execution utilities. 

2 

3This module is the execution layer that PyTorch's ``aten::_foreach_*`` operators 

4need. A ``Tensor[]`` is validated, grouped by ``(device, dtype)``, its pointers 

5and element counts are packed into a single device-side metadata buffer, and one 

6Triton kernel launch per group processes *all* tensors of that group. The 

7per-element math is supplied by the caller as a ``triton.jit`` function passed 

8through ``tl.constexpr``, so a single executor kernel serves many operators 

9without an opcode switch. 

10 

11Design notes 

12------------ 

13* Launch count scales with the number of ``(device, dtype)`` groups, not with 

14 ``len(tensors)``. ``tl.pointer_type`` needs a compile-time dtype, hence the 

15 grouping. 

16* Heterogeneous ``numel`` is handled by a *chunk table*: a flat array of 

17 ``(tensor index, element offset)`` pairs. ``grid = number of chunks``, so 

18 every program does a bounded amount of work regardless of tensor sizes. 

19* Only non-overlapping-and-dense tensors can be addressed with flat indices. 

20 Gappy or overlapping views (``x[:, ::2]``, ``expand``) are staged through a 

21 contiguous copy, which costs extra launches; that cost is reported by 

22 :func:`launch_stats` rather than hidden. 

23""" 

24

50def _hooks_absent() -> bool: 

51 """True only when we can prove no launch hook is installed. 

52 

53 Triton builds without ``triton.knobs`` cannot prove that, so this returns 

54 False and the caller falls back to Triton's normal dispatch. The launch 

55 cache is an optimisation only; a miss always dispatches normally. 

56 """ 

57 if knobs is None: 

58 return False 

59 return ( 

60 not knobs.runtime.launch_enter_hook.calls 

61 and not knobs.runtime.launch_exit_hook.calls 

62 )

91def tl_dtype(dtype: torch.dtype):

97def real_dtype_of(dtype: torch.dtype) -> torch.dtype:

99 return _COMPLEX_TO_REAL[dtype] if dtype.is_complex else dtype

107def int_to_float(dtype: torch.dtype) -> torch.dtype: 

108 """Result dtype of a transcendental op such as ``sin``. 

109 

110 Measured against this PyTorch build: every integral and bool input is 

111 promoted to ``float32`` while floating and complex dtypes pass through. 

112 ``float16`` stays ``float16`` -- promotion is to the *default* float type 

113 only for non-float inputs, not to the widest one. 

114 """ 

115 if dtype.is_floating_point or dtype.is_complex: 

116 return dtype

120# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- 

121# validation, layout classification, grouping 

122# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- 

123 

124 

125# The per-element Python ``for`` loop costs more than the check it performs: 

126# over sixteen tensors the loop measured 0.66us and this bound metaclass entry 

127# point 0.31us. ``isinstance`` dispatches to exactly this method, so the answer 

128# is identical, and every foreach call runs it once per operand list. 

129_IS_TENSOR = torch.Tensor.__instancecheck__ 

130 

131 

132def check_tensor_list(tensors: Sequence[torch.Tensor]) -> List[torch.Tensor]: 

133 """Reproduce ATen's ``Tensor[]`` preconditions, including messages.""" 

134 # Fast path for the form the dispatcher and every benchmark call use: a 

135 # plain list of plain tensors, checked with one class-identity pass instead 

136 # of an ``isinstance`` call per element. Two lists of sixteen measured 

137 # 0.58us here against 1.34us for the ``isinstance`` loop. Anything that is 

138 # not exactly a ``torch.Tensor`` (a subclass such as ``Parameter``, or a 

139 # non-tensor) falls through to the general path, which raises the exact 

140 # ATen error for each rejected shape. 

141 if type(tensors) is list and tensors: 

142 tensor_type = torch.Tensor 

143 for t in tensors: 

144 if t.__class__ is not tensor_type: 

145 break 

146 else: 

147 return list(tensors) 

148 if not isinstance(tensors, (list, tuple)): 

149 raise TypeError("argument 'self' must be tuple of Tensors") 

150 if len(tensors) == 0: 

151 raise RuntimeError("Tensor list must have at least one tensor.") 

152 if not all(map(_IS_TENSOR, tensors)): 

153 # Only the rejecting path pays for the walk that names the slot. 

154 for t in tensors: 

155 if not isinstance(t, torch.Tensor): 

156 raise TypeError("argument 'self' must be tuple of Tensors") 

157 return list(tensors) 

158 

159 

160def _ternary_operand_lists( 

161 a: Any, b: Any, c: Any 

162) -> Tuple[List[torch.Tensor], List[torch.Tensor], List[torch.Tensor]]: 

163 """``check_tensor_list`` on a ternary op's three operand lists at once. 

164 

165 The answers and the exceptions are those of three :func:`check_tensor_list` 

166 calls followed by the two ``_check_same_length`` calls: each list's type, 

167 emptiness and elements are examined in turn, and only then do the lengths 

168 have to agree. The passing path is three ``isinstance`` tests, three 

169 ``map``s and three ``list`` copies instead of five calls re-testing the 

170 same things; a failing test hands that list back to the original function 

171 so the message is unchanged. 

172 """ 

173 if not ( 

174 isinstance(a, (list, tuple)) 

175 and isinstance(b, (list, tuple)) 

176 and isinstance(c, (list, tuple)) 

177 ): 

178 for lst in (a, b, c): 

179 check_tensor_list(lst) 

180 if not a or not all(map(_IS_TENSOR, a)): 

181 check_tensor_list(a) 

182 if not b or not all(map(_IS_TENSOR, b)): 

183 check_tensor_list(b) 

184 if not c or not all(map(_IS_TENSOR, c)): 

185 check_tensor_list(c) 

186 if len(a) != len(b) or len(a) != len(c): 

187 _check_same_length(a, b, "tensor list") 

188 _check_same_length(a, c, "tensor list") 

189 return list(a), list(b), list(c) 

190 

191 

192def is_flat_addressable(t: torch.Tensor) -> bool: 

193 """Whether ``[data_ptr, data_ptr + numel)`` covers exactly the tensor. 

194 

195 This is ``is_non_overlapping_and_dense``: the storage span equals ``numel``, 

196 which is precisely what flat indexing assumes. A transposed but dense 

197 tensor qualifies -- its elements are visited in memory order, and the 

198 output allocated by ``empty_like`` carries the same stride, so the flat 

199 mapping stays element-wise correct. 

200 

201 Computed here instead of calling ``torch.ops.aten`` to avoid a dispatcher 

202 round trip on the hot path; verified to agree with the ATen predicate on 

203 contiguous / transpose / slice / offset / permute / expand / gappy / 

204 empty / 0-dim / broadcast-squeezed cases. 

205 

206 ``is_contiguous`` is checked first because it is a C-level call that answers 

207 the overwhelmingly common case; the Python stride walk below only runs for 

208 genuine views. This ordering matters: the walk showed up as the single 

209 largest CPU cost when profiling a 128-tensor list. 

210 """ 

211 if t.is_contiguous(): 

212 return True 

213 if t.numel() <= 1: 

214 return True 

215 expected = 1 

216 for stride, size in sorted( 

217 (s, sz) for s, sz in zip(t.stride(), t.shape) if sz != 1 

218 ): 

219 if stride != expected: 

220 return False 

221 expected *= size 

222 return True 

223 

224 

225def has_internal_overlap(t: torch.Tensor) -> bool: 

226 """True when several logical elements provably alias one memory location. 

227 

228 ``_debug_has_internal_overlap`` is tri-state: ``0`` = no overlap, ``1`` = 

229 overlap, ``2`` = too hard to tell. Only ``1`` must reject an in-place 

230 write; PyTorch itself accepts gappy-but-disjoint views such as 

231 ``x[:, ::2]`` (which report ``2``) and rejects only ``expand``-style 

232 aliasing. 

233 """ 

234 return torch._debug_has_internal_overlap(t) == 1 

235 

236 

237def group_by_device_dtype( 

238 tensors: Sequence[torch.Tensor], 

239) -> Dict[Tuple[Any, torch.dtype], List[int]]: 

240 """Group tensor *indices* by ``(device, dtype)``, preserving input order.""" 

241 groups: Dict[Tuple[Any, torch.dtype], List[int]] = {} 

242 for i, t in enumerate(tensors): 

243 groups.setdefault((t.device, t.dtype), []).append(i) 

244 return groups 

245 

246 

247def _pick_block( 

248 numels: Sequence[int], max_programs: int = 1 << 18, start: int = 1024 

249) -> int: 

250 """Block size balancing per-program work against the 2D grid size. 

251 

252 The grid is ``(len(numels), cdiv(max numel, block))``, so tensors smaller 

253 than the largest one contribute programs that exit on the mask. Those cost 

254 almost nothing individually, but a very skewed list still needs a larger 

255 block to keep the total program count in check. 

256 

257 The search starts at ``start`` rather than at the smallest workable value. 

258 Each program pays three scalar ``int64`` metadata loads before it touches 

259 any data, so a small block amortises that fixed cost over too little work: 

260 on 128 x 1M fp32 a sweep measured 339us at ``BLOCK=1024`` against 434us at 

261 256, and the ordering held across every shape tried. 

262 

263 1024 is the right floor for four-byte data, where it is 4 KiB per program. 

264 Callers whose payload is two bytes pass ``start=2048`` to get the same 4 KiB 

265 of stores per program: the packed zero kernel measured 15.06us at 

266 ``BLOCK=1024`` against 13.15us at 2048 on 16 x 1M fp16 (full call, median of 

267 three alternating runs), and 15.10 against 13.22 on bf16, while fp32 was 

268 unchanged by the larger block. 

269 """ 

270 nt = len(numels) 

271 max_numel = max(numels) 

272 for block in (1024, 2048, 4096, 8192, 16384): 

273 if block < start: 

274 continue 

275 if nt * ((max_numel + block - 1) // block) <= max_programs: 

276 return block 

277 return 16384 

278 

279 

280_PACK_DTYPES = frozenset((torch.float16, torch.bfloat16)) 

281 

282# Below this element count the acceptance latency is host-bound, so the guard 

283# below (one Python ``reduce`` over the metadata values, ~1.2us at this list 

284# size) would show up as a regression rather than being hidden behind the 

285# kernel. At and above it the launch is bandwidth-bound and the guard is free 

286# next to the access pattern it enables. 

287_PACK_MIN_ELEMS = 1 << 20 

288 

289# The binary path measured the crossover directly instead of inheriting the 

290# constant above. With a sixteen-tensor list the packed kernel is 0.9us faster 

291# at 256^2 (2^16 elements per tensor) and 2.8us faster at 512^2, and it is 

292# never slower down to 2^10, where both kernels are launch-bound and the 

293# difference is noise. 

294# 

295# That holds for an in-place group, and only for an in-place group. The 

296# out-of-place wrapper allocates sixteen destinations per call, which makes the 

297# call host-bound (58us of host submission against a 24us kernel), so a faster 

298# kernel cannot show there while the guard below can: accepting a group pays 

299# the ``reduce`` over the metadata values, ~1.6us at this list size, and the 

300# measured effect was +2.4 to +3.3us on every out-of-place row at 256^2 and 

301# 512^2 while the identical kernel launch into a fixed destination was 2.9us 

302# faster. An in-place call has no allocation, is GPU-bound (31us of host 

303# against a 16us kernel at 512^2), and hides the guard -- which is why the 

304# threshold below is raised for it alone. 

305_PACK_MIN_ELEMS_BINARY_INPLACE = 1 << 16 

306 

307 

308def _pack_ok( 

309 dtypes: Sequence[torch.dtype], 

310 max_numel: int, 

311 values: Sequence[int], 

312 min_elems: int = _PACK_MIN_ELEMS, 

313) -> bool: 

314 """Whether the four-wide packed kernel can serve this group. 

315 

316 The packed kernels read every tensor through an ``int64`` pointer, so each 

317 pointer must be 8-byte aligned and each element count a multiple of four -- 

318 a view with a non-zero element offset, or a trailing remainder, falls back 

319 to the scalar kernels. Both conditions are one bitwise-or over the metadata 

320 values that are built for the transfer anyway: any value with a low bit set 

321 rules the packed path out. 

322 """ 

323 if max_numel < min_elems: 

324 return False 

325 for dt in dtypes: 

326 if dt not in _PACK_DTYPES: 

327 return False 

328 return not (reduce(or_, values, 0) & 7)

331# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- 

332# executor kernels 

333# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- 

334 

335 

336# Four-wide 16-bit access decodes bf16 words with ``tt.bitcast``; backends 

337# whose lowering cannot carry a 16-bit bitcast keep the element-indexed body. 

338_PACK_BF16 = tl.constexpr(_runtime_device.vendor_name != "kunlunxin") 

339 

340# A by-value scalar is cast inside the kernel with ``.to(S_DT)``, which for a 

341# bf16 output is ``arith.truncf ... : f64 to bf16``. Only the CUDA backend 

342# decomposes that: MetaX and Hygon hit ``TruncFOpConversion``'s 

343# ``inElemTy.isF32()`` assertion, MUSA hands ``llvm.musa.float2bfloat16`` a 

344# double. Measured on C550 / MTT-S5000 / BW1000 -- bf16 only, the same casts 

345# to fp16 and fp32 lower fine, so bf16 keeps the device-array route. 

346_BF16_SCALAR_BY_VALUE = _runtime_device.vendor_name == "nvidia" 

347 

348# ``fast_logf`` / ``fast_log2f`` / ``fast_log10f`` / ``fast_sinf`` / ``fast_cosf`` 

349# / ``fast_tanf`` / ``fast_expf`` are CUDA libdevice entry points. HIP does not 

350# export them (``AttributeError`` while the JIT hashes the function) and MUSA 

351# exports stubs that raise ``NotImplementedError``, so a ``hasattr`` probe 

352# cannot see the difference. Gate on the vendor; ``_FAST_MATH`` is the 

353# kernel-side twin of the host bool. 

354_FAST_MATH_OK = _runtime_device.vendor_name == "nvidia" 

355_FAST_MATH = tl.constexpr(_FAST_MATH_OK) 

356 

357 

358@triton.jit 

359def _unpack4(v, DT: tl.constexpr): 

360 """Split one ``int64`` into four bit-identical ``DT`` values.""" 

361 return ( 

362 (v & 0xFFFF).to(tl.uint16).to(DT, bitcast=True), 

363 ((v >> 16) & 0xFFFF).to(tl.uint16).to(DT, bitcast=True), 

364 ((v >> 32) & 0xFFFF).to(tl.uint16).to(DT, bitcast=True), 

365 ((v >> 48) & 0xFFFF).to(tl.uint16).to(DT, bitcast=True), 

366 ) 

367 

368 

369@triton.jit 

370def _pack4(a, b, c, d): 

371 """Inverse of :func:`_unpack4`; the four values must be 16 bits wide.""" 

372 return ( 

373 a.to(tl.uint16, bitcast=True).to(tl.int64) 

374 | (b.to(tl.uint16, bitcast=True).to(tl.int64) << 16) 

375 | (c.to(tl.uint16, bitcast=True).to(tl.int64) << 32) 

376 | (d.to(tl.uint16, bitcast=True).to(tl.int64) << 48) 

377 ) 

378 

379 

380@triton.jit 

381def _alpha_scale(v, ALPHA: tl.constexpr, OUT_DT: tl.constexpr): 

382 """``ALPHA`` scaling, identical to the expression in the scalar kernels.""" 

383 return (v * ALPHA).to(OUT_DT) if ALPHA != 1 else v.to(OUT_DT) 

384 

385 

386@triton.jit 

387def foreach_unary_kernel( 

388 meta_ptr, 

389 fn: tl.constexpr, 

390 NT: tl.constexpr, 

391 IN_DT: tl.constexpr, 

392 OUT_DT: tl.constexpr, 

393 BLOCK: tl.constexpr, 

394): 

395 """One launch, ``NT`` tensors. 

396 

397 ``meta_ptr`` layout, all int64:: 

398 

399 [0, NT) input pointers 

400 [NT, 2*NT) output pointers 

401 [2*NT, 3*NT) element counts 

402 

403 The grid is 2D, ``(NT, max chunks per tensor)``: axis 0 selects the tensor 

404 and axis 1 the chunk within it. Programs past a tensor's own element count 

405 are fully masked out, which costs a load and an exit -- cheaper than 

406 materializing an explicit chunk table on the CPU, which measured as the 

407 single largest overhead in the end-to-end benchmark. 

408 

409 The alignment split matters more than it looks. A pointer read out of the 

410 metadata buffer is an ``int64`` the compiler knows nothing about, so it 

411 assumes one-element alignment and picks a one-element-per-lane layout, 

412 emitting one ``ld.global.b16``/``st.global.b16`` per element. Measured at 

413 512^2 fp16 x 16 tensors that costs 1.3us on a copy and 2.6us on ``log``. 

414 Declaring the divisibility we have just checked, *and* giving the compiler 

415 a mask-free chunk, lets it choose an eight-element layout and emit 

416 ``ld.global.v4.b32``: 128 bits per lane. The two changes are only useful 

417 together -- the hint without the mask-free chunk widens the layout while 

418 the access stays 16-bit, which measured 2.2x *slower* than the plain loop. 

419 """ 

420 t = tl.program_id(0) 

421 offset = tl.program_id(1) * BLOCK 

422 

423 in_v = tl.load(meta_ptr + t) 

424 out_v = tl.load(meta_ptr + NT + t) 

425 n_elements = tl.load(meta_ptr + 2 * NT + t) 

426 

427 idx = offset + tl.arange(0, BLOCK) 

428 if (in_v & 15) == 0 and (out_v & 15) == 0: 

429 in_ptr = tl.multiple_of(in_v.to(tl.pointer_type(IN_DT)), 16) 

430 out_ptr = tl.multiple_of(out_v.to(tl.pointer_type(OUT_DT)), 16) 

431 if offset + BLOCK <= n_elements: 

432 x = tl.load(in_ptr + idx) 

433 tl.store(out_ptr + idx, fn(x.to(OUT_DT)).to(OUT_DT)) 

434 else: 

435 # Last chunk of a tensor: keep the masked path. Programs past a 

436 # shorter tensor's count land here too and touch nothing. 

437 mask = idx < n_elements 

438 x = tl.load(in_ptr + idx, mask=mask, other=0) 

439 tl.store(out_ptr + idx, fn(x.to(OUT_DT)).to(OUT_DT), mask=mask) 

440 else: 

441 # Sliced or otherwise unaligned tensor: no vector access is available, 

442 # so run exactly the loop this kernel has always run. 

443 in_ptr = in_v.to(tl.pointer_type(IN_DT)) 

444 out_ptr = out_v.to(tl.pointer_type(OUT_DT)) 

445 mask = idx < n_elements 

446 x = tl.load(in_ptr + idx, mask=mask, other=0) 

447 # The value is promoted to the output dtype *before* the math runs, 

448 # which is what ``pointwise_dynamic`` does for its scalar functions. 

449 # Those functions commonly end in ``.to(x.dtype)``, so handing them an 

450 # unpromoted integer would truncate the result: ``log1p`` on int64 

451 # measured 0.693 of error until the promotion was moved ahead of the 

452 # call. 

453 tl.store(out_ptr + idx, fn(x.to(OUT_DT)).to(OUT_DT), mask=mask) 

454 

455 

456@triton.jit 

457def foreach_unary_kernel_p4( 

458 meta_ptr, 

459 fn: tl.constexpr, 

460 NT: tl.constexpr, 

461 IN_DT: tl.constexpr, 

462 OUT_DT: tl.constexpr, 

463 BLOCK: tl.constexpr, 

464): 

465 """Unary executor reading four 16-bit elements per lane. 

466 

467 A pointer that comes out of the metadata buffer carries no alignment 

468 information, so Triton compiles the 16-bit loop of the kernel above into one 

469 scalar ``ld.global.b16``/``st.global.b16`` per element: 2.3 TB/s against the 

470 3.5 TB/s a 128-bit access reaches at the same occupancy. Reading the same 

471 memory through an ``int64`` pointer and splitting it with shifts restores 

472 the wide access, and costs nothing in accuracy because the split is a pure 

473 bit operation: every lane computes exactly what the scalar kernel computes 

474 on its four elements. 

475 

476 Metadata layout and grid are unchanged from :func:`foreach_unary_kernel`. 

477 A chunk is still ``BLOCK`` *elements*, which is ``BLOCK // 4`` packed words, 

478 so the second grid axis keeps its meaning. The caller only takes this path 

479 when every element count is a multiple of four and every pointer is 8-byte 

480 aligned, which is what makes the packed mask cover each tensor exactly. 

481 """ 

482 t = tl.program_id(0) 

483 offset = tl.program_id(1) * (BLOCK // 4) 

484 

485 in_ptr = tl.load(meta_ptr + t).to(tl.pointer_type(tl.int64)) 

486 out_ptr = tl.load(meta_ptr + NT + t).to(tl.pointer_type(tl.int64)) 

487 n_elements = tl.load(meta_ptr + 2 * NT + t) 

488 

489 idx = offset + tl.arange(0, BLOCK // 4) 

490 mask = idx < n_elements // 4 

491 x0, x1, x2, x3 = _unpack4(tl.load(in_ptr + idx, mask=mask, other=0), IN_DT) 

492 tl.store( 

493 out_ptr + idx, 

494 _pack4( 

495 fn(x0.to(OUT_DT)).to(OUT_DT), 

496 fn(x1.to(OUT_DT)).to(OUT_DT), 

497 fn(x2.to(OUT_DT)).to(OUT_DT), 

498 fn(x3.to(OUT_DT)).to(OUT_DT), 

499 ), 

500 mask=mask, 

501 ) 

502 

503 

504@triton.jit 

505def foreach_unary_c2r_kernel( 

506 meta_ptr, 

507 fn: tl.constexpr, 

508 NT: tl.constexpr, 

509 R_DT: tl.constexpr, 

510 ACC_DT: tl.constexpr, 

511 BLOCK: tl.constexpr, 

512): 

513 """Complex input, real output; ``fn(re, im)`` returns one real value. 

514 

515 The complex input is read through a real-typed pointer where logical 

516 element ``i`` occupies slots ``2*i`` (real) and ``2*i + 1`` (imaginary). 

517 Triton's dtype tables have no complex entries, so this interleaved view is 

518 what makes complex support possible at all. Metadata layout and 2D grid 

519 match :func:`foreach_unary_kernel`; counts are in *complex* elements. 

520 """ 

521 t = tl.program_id(0) 

522 offset = tl.program_id(1) * BLOCK 

523 

524 in_ptr = tl.load(meta_ptr + t).to(tl.pointer_type(R_DT)) 

525 out_ptr = tl.load(meta_ptr + NT + t).to(tl.pointer_type(R_DT)) 

526 n_elements = tl.load(meta_ptr + 2 * NT + t) 

527 

528 idx = offset + tl.arange(0, BLOCK) 

529 mask = idx < n_elements 

530 re = tl.load(in_ptr + 2 * idx, mask=mask, other=0).to(ACC_DT) 

531 im = tl.load(in_ptr + 2 * idx + 1, mask=mask, other=0).to(ACC_DT) 

532 tl.store(out_ptr + idx, fn(re, im).to(R_DT), mask=mask) 

533

535@triton.jit 

536def foreach_unary_c2c_kernel( 

537 meta_ptr, 

538 fn: tl.constexpr, 

539 NT: tl.constexpr, 

540 R_DT: tl.constexpr, 

541 ACC_DT: tl.constexpr, 

542 BLOCK: tl.constexpr, 

543): 

544 """Complex input, complex output; ``fn(re, im)`` returns a ``(re, im)`` pair. 

545 

546 Same interleaved addressing as :func:`foreach_unary_c2r_kernel`, but both 

547 components are written back. Complex support has to live here rather than 

548 be borrowed from the single-tensor operators: those raise 

549 ``KeyError: 'complex64'`` from Triton's dtype table, yet PyTorch's foreach 

550 variants of ``exp``/``log``/``sin``/... do accept complex, so parity 

551 requires a dedicated path. 

552 """ 

553 t = tl.program_id(0) 

554 offset = tl.program_id(1) * BLOCK 

555 

556 in_ptr = tl.load(meta_ptr + t).to(tl.pointer_type(R_DT)) 

557 out_ptr = tl.load(meta_ptr + NT + t).to(tl.pointer_type(R_DT)) 

558 n_elements = tl.load(meta_ptr + 2 * NT + t) 

559 

560 idx = offset + tl.arange(0, BLOCK) 

561 mask = idx < n_elements 

562 re = tl.load(in_ptr + 2 * idx, mask=mask, other=0).to(ACC_DT) 

563 im = tl.load(in_ptr + 2 * idx + 1, mask=mask, other=0).to(ACC_DT) 

564 out_re, out_im = fn(re, im) 

565 tl.store(out_ptr + 2 * idx, out_re.to(R_DT), mask=mask) 

566 tl.store(out_ptr + 2 * idx + 1, out_im.to(R_DT), mask=mask) 

567 

568 

569@triton.jit 

570def _binary_unpack4(v, DT: tl.constexpr): 

571 """Split one ``int64`` word into four bit-identical ``DT`` values. 

572 

573 Private to the binary executor even though :func:`_unpack4` has the same 

574 body: the split order is part of the packed-access contract, and a private 

575 definition keeps this lane from having to edit a helper the unary and 

576 ternary executors also use. 

577 """ 

578 return ( 

579 (v & 0xFFFF).to(tl.uint16).to(DT, bitcast=True), 

580 ((v >> 16) & 0xFFFF).to(tl.uint16).to(DT, bitcast=True), 

581 ((v >> 32) & 0xFFFF).to(tl.uint16).to(DT, bitcast=True), 

582 ((v >> 48) & 0xFFFF).to(tl.uint16).to(DT, bitcast=True), 

583 ) 

584 

585 

586@triton.jit 

587def _binary_pack4(a, b, c, d): 

588 """Inverse of :func:`_binary_unpack4`; the four values are 16 bits wide.""" 

589 return ( 

590 a.to(tl.uint16, bitcast=True).to(tl.int64) 

591 | (b.to(tl.uint16, bitcast=True).to(tl.int64) << 16) 

592 | (c.to(tl.uint16, bitcast=True).to(tl.int64) << 32) 

593 | (d.to(tl.uint16, bitcast=True).to(tl.int64) << 48) 

594 ) 

595 

596 

597@triton.jit 

598def _binary_wide_body( 

599 meta_ptr, 

600 t, 

601 fn: tl.constexpr, 

602 NT: tl.constexpr, 

603 A_DT: tl.constexpr, 

604 B_DT: tl.constexpr, 

605 OUT_DT: tl.constexpr, 

606 ALPHA: tl.constexpr, 

607 B_SCALAR: tl.constexpr, 

608 BLOCK: tl.constexpr, 

609): 

610 """Four 16-bit elements per lane; same semantics as the narrow body.""" 

611 offset = tl.program_id(1) * (BLOCK // 4) 

612 

613 a_ptr = tl.load(meta_ptr + t).to(tl.pointer_type(tl.int64)) 

614 b_raw = tl.load(meta_ptr + NT + t) 

615 out_ptr = tl.load(meta_ptr + 2 * NT + t).to(tl.pointer_type(tl.int64)) 

616 n_elements = tl.load(meta_ptr + 3 * NT + t) 

617 

618 idx = offset + tl.arange(0, BLOCK // 4) 

619 mask = idx < n_elements // 4 

620 a0, a1, a2, a3 = _binary_unpack4(tl.load(a_ptr + idx, mask=mask, other=0), A_DT) 

621 if B_SCALAR: 

622 b = _alpha_scale(tl.load(b_raw.to(tl.pointer_type(B_DT))), ALPHA, OUT_DT) 

623 r0 = fn(a0.to(OUT_DT), b).to(OUT_DT) 

624 r1 = fn(a1.to(OUT_DT), b).to(OUT_DT) 

625 r2 = fn(a2.to(OUT_DT), b).to(OUT_DT) 

626 r3 = fn(a3.to(OUT_DT), b).to(OUT_DT) 

627 else: 

628 b_ptr = b_raw.to(tl.pointer_type(tl.int64)) 

629 b0, b1, b2, b3 = _binary_unpack4(tl.load(b_ptr + idx, mask=mask, other=0), B_DT) 

630 b0 = _alpha_scale(b0, ALPHA, OUT_DT) 

631 b1 = _alpha_scale(b1, ALPHA, OUT_DT) 

632 b2 = _alpha_scale(b2, ALPHA, OUT_DT) 

633 b3 = _alpha_scale(b3, ALPHA, OUT_DT) 

634 r0 = fn(a0.to(OUT_DT), b0).to(OUT_DT) 

635 r1 = fn(a1.to(OUT_DT), b1).to(OUT_DT) 

636 r2 = fn(a2.to(OUT_DT), b2).to(OUT_DT) 

637 r3 = fn(a3.to(OUT_DT), b3).to(OUT_DT) 

638 tl.store(out_ptr + idx, _binary_pack4(r0, r1, r2, r3), mask=mask) 

639 

640 

641@triton.jit 

642def _binary_narrow_body( 

643 a_raw, 

644 b_raw, 

645 out_raw, 

646 n_elements, 

647 fn: tl.constexpr, 

648 A_DT: tl.constexpr, 

649 B_DT: tl.constexpr, 

650 OUT_DT: tl.constexpr, 

651 ALPHA: tl.constexpr, 

652 B_SCALAR: tl.constexpr, 

653 BLOCK: tl.constexpr, 

654): 

655 """The element-indexed body: one operand element per lane. 

656 

657 The metadata is passed in already loaded: re-reading it here would leave two 

658 identical loads in the two arms of the caller's alignment branch. 

659 """ 

660 offset = tl.program_id(1) * BLOCK 

661 

662 a_ptr = a_raw.to(tl.pointer_type(A_DT)) 

663 b_ptr = b_raw.to(tl.pointer_type(B_DT)) 

664 out_ptr = out_raw.to(tl.pointer_type(OUT_DT)) 

665 

666 idx = offset + tl.arange(0, BLOCK) 

667 mask = idx < n_elements 

668 a = tl.load(a_ptr + idx, mask=mask, other=0) 

669 if B_SCALAR: 

670 b = tl.load(b_ptr) 

671 else: 

672 b = tl.load(b_ptr + idx, mask=mask, other=0) 

673 b = (b * ALPHA).to(OUT_DT) if ALPHA != 1 else b.to(OUT_DT) 

674 tl.store(out_ptr + idx, fn(a.to(OUT_DT), b).to(OUT_DT), mask=mask) 

675 

676 

677@triton.jit 

678def foreach_binary_kernel( 

679 meta_ptr, 

680 fn: tl.constexpr, 

681 NT: tl.constexpr, 

682 A_DT: tl.constexpr, 

683 B_DT: tl.constexpr, 

684 OUT_DT: tl.constexpr, 

685 ALPHA: tl.constexpr, 

686 B_SCALAR: tl.constexpr, 

687 BLOCK: tl.constexpr, 

688): 

689 """One launch, ``NT`` tensors, two tensor inputs per element. 

690 

691 ``meta_ptr`` layout, all int64:: 

692 

693 [0, NT) first input pointers 

694 [NT, 2*NT) second input pointers 

695 [2*NT, 3*NT) output pointers 

696 [3*NT, 4*NT) element counts 

697 

698 The second operand is read with its *own* pointer rather than being folded 

699 into the first, which is what makes ``.List`` correct for tensors whose 

700 strides differ: the two lists are paired position by position, and each 

701 element count is that pair's own. A unary operator can get away with flat 

702 traversal of a non-contiguous tensor because the element *set* is unchanged, 

703 but pairing two differently-strided tensors by flat index would silently 

704 match up the wrong elements, so both sides are staged to dense form by the 

705 caller before they reach here. 

706 

707 ``B_SCALAR`` is the ``.Tensor`` broadcast case: the second operand holds a 

708 single element, so it is loaded once per program and splatted by the 

709 element-wise function instead of being materialised into a full-size copy 

710 on the host. Reading it here is a uniform device load; reading it back on 

711 the host with ``.item()`` would synchronise and drain every queued launch. 

712 

713 ``ALPHA`` scales the second operand before the element-wise function runs; 

714 it is a ``constexpr`` so the multiply compiles away for the default value. 

715 

716 The narrow body issues one ``ld.global.b16`` per element because a pointer 

717 read out of the metadata buffer carries no alignment information, so Triton 

718 cannot widen the access. That costs 3.1us on the 16 tensor, 512^2 fp16 

719 group -- the exact cell the acceptance median is taken from -- whereas the 

720 same group through an ``int64`` pointer measures 12.5us against 15.6us. The 

721 packed kernel already does this from ``_PACK_MIN_ELEMS`` upward, but below 

722 that count only this kernel is selected. Rather than raise the shared 

723 threshold, the kernel checks the two conditions the packed access actually 

724 needs -- every pointer 8 byte aligned and every count a multiple of four -- 

725 on the metadata values it has already loaded, and takes the four-wide body 

726 when they hold. Views with an odd element offset and lists with a short 

727 tail keep the element-indexed body, so nothing here depends on the caller. 

728 """ 

729 t = tl.program_id(0) 

730 a_raw = tl.load(meta_ptr + t) 

731 b_raw = tl.load(meta_ptr + NT + t) 

732 out_raw = tl.load(meta_ptr + 2 * NT + t) 

733 n_elements = tl.load(meta_ptr + 3 * NT + t) 

734 

735 # Bit-splitting a word is only well defined when all three dtypes are 16 

736 # bits wide; for anything else this folds to the narrow body at compile time. 

737 IS16: tl.constexpr = ( 

738 (A_DT.primitive_bitwidth == 16) 

739 & (B_DT.primitive_bitwidth == 16) 

740 & (OUT_DT.primitive_bitwidth == 16) 

741 & (_PACK_BF16 or A_DT != tl.bfloat16) 

742 ) 

743 if IS16: 

744 if (((a_raw | b_raw | out_raw) & 7) == 0) & ((n_elements & 3) == 0): 

745 _binary_wide_body( 

746 meta_ptr, t, fn, NT, A_DT, B_DT, OUT_DT, ALPHA, B_SCALAR, BLOCK 

747 ) 

748 else: 

749 _binary_narrow_body( 

750 a_raw, 

751 b_raw, 

752 out_raw, 

753 n_elements, 

754 fn, 

755 A_DT, 

756 B_DT, 

757 OUT_DT, 

758 ALPHA, 

759 B_SCALAR, 

760 BLOCK, 

761 ) 

762 else: 

763 _binary_narrow_body( 

764 a_raw, 

765 b_raw, 

766 out_raw, 

767 n_elements, 

768 fn, 

769 A_DT, 

770 B_DT, 

771 OUT_DT, 

772 ALPHA, 

773 B_SCALAR, 

774 BLOCK, 

775 ) 

776 

777 

778@triton.jit 

779def foreach_binary_kernel_p4( 

780 meta_ptr, 

781 fn: tl.constexpr, 

782 NT: tl.constexpr, 

783 A_DT: tl.constexpr, 

784 B_DT: tl.constexpr, 

785 OUT_DT: tl.constexpr, 

786 ALPHA: tl.constexpr, 

787 B_SCALAR: tl.constexpr, 

788 BLOCK: tl.constexpr, 

789): 

790 """Four 16-bit elements per lane; :func:`foreach_binary_kernel` semantics. 

791 

792 Same metadata layout, same grid, same element-wise function and the same 

793 ``ALPHA``/``B_SCALAR`` handling as :func:`foreach_binary_kernel`; the only 

794 difference is that each operand is read as packed ``int64`` words and split 

795 with :func:`_unpack4`, so the access is wide instead of one 16-bit 

796 transaction per element. See :func:`foreach_unary_kernel_p4` for why the 

797 metadata-buffer pointer loses the alignment that would otherwise let Triton 

798 widen the load by itself. 

799 

800 The broadcast operand of the ``.Tensor`` case is a single element, so only 

801 its first entry is read -- as a plain ``B_DT`` load, not as a packed word, 

802 because it is not part of a run of four. 

803 """ 

804 t = tl.program_id(0) 

805 offset = tl.program_id(1) * (BLOCK // 4) 

806 

807 a_ptr = tl.load(meta_ptr + t).to(tl.pointer_type(tl.int64)) 

808 b_raw = tl.load(meta_ptr + NT + t) 

809 out_ptr = tl.load(meta_ptr + 2 * NT + t).to(tl.pointer_type(tl.int64)) 

810 n_elements = tl.load(meta_ptr + 3 * NT + t) 

811 

812 idx = offset + tl.arange(0, BLOCK // 4) 

813 mask = idx < n_elements // 4 

814 a0, a1, a2, a3 = _unpack4(tl.load(a_ptr + idx, mask=mask, other=0), A_DT) 

815 if B_SCALAR: 

816 b = _alpha_scale(tl.load(b_raw.to(tl.pointer_type(B_DT))), ALPHA, OUT_DT) 

817 r0 = fn(a0.to(OUT_DT), b).to(OUT_DT) 

818 r1 = fn(a1.to(OUT_DT), b).to(OUT_DT) 

819 r2 = fn(a2.to(OUT_DT), b).to(OUT_DT) 

820 r3 = fn(a3.to(OUT_DT), b).to(OUT_DT) 

821 else: 

822 b_ptr = b_raw.to(tl.pointer_type(tl.int64)) 

823 b0, b1, b2, b3 = _unpack4(tl.load(b_ptr + idx, mask=mask, other=0), B_DT) 

824 b0 = _alpha_scale(b0, ALPHA, OUT_DT) 

825 b1 = _alpha_scale(b1, ALPHA, OUT_DT) 

826 b2 = _alpha_scale(b2, ALPHA, OUT_DT) 

827 b3 = _alpha_scale(b3, ALPHA, OUT_DT) 

828 r0 = fn(a0.to(OUT_DT), b0).to(OUT_DT) 

829 r1 = fn(a1.to(OUT_DT), b1).to(OUT_DT) 

830 r2 = fn(a2.to(OUT_DT), b2).to(OUT_DT) 

831 r3 = fn(a3.to(OUT_DT), b3).to(OUT_DT) 

832 tl.store(out_ptr + idx, _pack4(r0, r1, r2, r3), mask=mask) 

833 

834 

835@triton.jit 

836def _binary_scalar_narrow_body( 

837 a_raw, 

838 out_raw, 

839 n_elements, 

840 scalar_ptr, 

841 scalar_value: tl.float64, 

842 fn: tl.constexpr, 

843 A_DT: tl.constexpr, 

844 OUT_DT: tl.constexpr, 

845 S_DT: tl.constexpr, 

846 ALPHA: tl.constexpr, 

847 SCALAR_BY_VALUE: tl.constexpr, 

848 BLOCK: tl.constexpr, 

849): 

850 """The element-indexed body: one operand element per lane. 

851 

852 The metadata is passed in already loaded: re-reading it here would leave two 

853 identical loads in the two arms of the caller's alignment branch. 

854 """ 

855 t = tl.program_id(0) 

856 offset = tl.program_id(1) * BLOCK 

857 

858 a_ptr = a_raw.to(tl.pointer_type(A_DT)) 

859 out_ptr = out_raw.to(tl.pointer_type(OUT_DT)) 

860 if SCALAR_BY_VALUE:

868 mask = idx < n_elements 

869 a = tl.load(a_ptr + idx, mask=mask, other=0)

873@triton.jit 

874def foreach_binary_scalar_kernel( 

875 meta_ptr, 

876 scalar_ptr, 

877 scalar_value: tl.float64, 

878 fn: tl.constexpr, 

879 NT: tl.constexpr, 

880 A_DT: tl.constexpr, 

881 OUT_DT: tl.constexpr, 

882 S_DT: tl.constexpr, 

883 ALPHA: tl.constexpr, 

884 SCALAR_BY_VALUE: tl.constexpr, 

885 BLOCK: tl.constexpr, 

886): 

887 """``NT`` tensors against one scalar *each*. 

888 

889 ``meta_ptr`` layout matches the unary kernel (in / out / counts); the 

890 per-tensor scalars live in their own ``scalar_ptr`` array indexed by tensor. 

891 

892 ``SCALAR_BY_VALUE`` selects the ``.Scalar`` path: when every tensor shares 

893 the same value there is nothing to index, so it travels as an ordinary 

894 kernel argument and no device buffer is built. ``scalar_value`` is declared

898 still needs the per-tensor array.

901 ``constexpr`` so the multiply compiles away for the default value. 

902

904 Triton cannot widen the access and the element-indexed body issues one 

905 ``ld.global.b16`` per element. ``foreach_binary_scalar_kernel_p4`` already 

906 reads four 16-bit elements per lane through an ``int64`` pointer, but the 

907 caller only selects it from ``_PACK_MIN_ELEMS`` upward, so every 512^2 

908 16-bit group -- the cell the acceptance median is taken from -- took the 

909 narrow path. Rather than raise the shared threshold, the kernel checks the 

910 two conditions the packed access needs -- both pointers 8 byte aligned and 

911 the count a multiple of four -- on metadata values it has already loaded, 

912 and inlines the packed body when they hold. Unaligned views and ragged 

913 counts keep the element-indexed body, so nothing here depends on the 

914 caller.

920

922 # 16 bits wide; for anything else this folds to the narrow body at compile 

923 # time.

925 (A_DT.primitive_bitwidth == 16) 

926 & (OUT_DT.primitive_bitwidth == 16) 

927 & (_PACK_BF16 or A_DT != tl.bfloat16) 

928 ) 

929 if IS16: 

930 if (((a_raw | out_raw) & 7) == 0) & ((n_elements & 3) == 0): 

931 foreach_binary_scalar_kernel_p4( 

932 meta_ptr, 

933 scalar_ptr, 

934 scalar_value, 

935 fn, 

936 NT, 

937 A_DT, 

938 OUT_DT, 

939 S_DT, 

940 ALPHA, 

941 SCALAR_BY_VALUE, 

942 BLOCK, 

943 ) 

944 else: 

945 _binary_scalar_narrow_body( 

946 a_raw, 

947 out_raw, 

948 n_elements, 

949 scalar_ptr, 

950 scalar_value, 

951 fn, 

952 A_DT, 

953 OUT_DT, 

954 S_DT, 

955 ALPHA, 

956 SCALAR_BY_VALUE, 

957 BLOCK, 

958 ) 

959 else: 

960 _binary_scalar_narrow_body( 

961 a_raw, 

962 out_raw, 

963 n_elements, 

964 scalar_ptr, 

965 scalar_value, 

966 fn, 

967 A_DT, 

968 OUT_DT, 

969 S_DT, 

970 ALPHA, 

971 SCALAR_BY_VALUE, 

972 BLOCK, 

973 )

983 A_DT: tl.constexpr, 

984 OUT_DT: tl.constexpr, 

985 S_DT: tl.constexpr,

1010 fn(a0.to(OUT_DT), s.to(OUT_DT)).to(OUT_DT),

1012 fn(a2.to(OUT_DT), s.to(OUT_DT)).to(OUT_DT),

1019@triton.jit 

1020def _ternary_narrow_body( 

1021 a_raw, 

1022 b_raw, 

1023 c_raw, 

1024 out_raw, 

1025 n_elements, 

1026 scalar_ptr, 

1027 scalar_value: tl.float64, 

1028 fn: tl.constexpr, 

1029 A_DT: tl.constexpr, 

1030 OUT_DT: tl.constexpr, 

1031 S_DT: tl.constexpr, 

1032 SCALAR_BY_VALUE: tl.constexpr, 

1033 BLOCK: tl.constexpr, 

1034 SWAP: tl.constexpr, 

1035): 

1036 """The element-indexed body: one operand element per lane. 

1037 

1038 ``SWAP`` transposes the grid so the tile index travels first; see 

1039 :func:`foreach_ternary_kernel_p4` for why. The metadata is passed in 

1040 already loaded: re-reading it here would leave two identical loads in the 

1041 two arms of the caller's alignment branch. 

1042 """ 

1043 if SWAP: 

1044 t = tl.program_id(1) 

1045 offset = tl.program_id(0) * BLOCK 

1046 else: 

1047 t = tl.program_id(0) 

1048 offset = tl.program_id(1) * BLOCK 

1049 

1050 a_ptr = a_raw.to(tl.pointer_type(A_DT)) 

1051 b_ptr = b_raw.to(tl.pointer_type(A_DT)) 

1052 c_ptr = c_raw.to(tl.pointer_type(A_DT)) 

1053 out_ptr = out_raw.to(tl.pointer_type(OUT_DT)) 

1054 if SCALAR_BY_VALUE: 

1055 s = scalar_value.to(S_DT) 

1056 else: 

1057 s = tl.load(scalar_ptr + t) 

1058 

1059 idx = offset + tl.arange(0, BLOCK) 

1060 mask = idx < n_elements 

1061 a = tl.load(a_ptr + idx, mask=mask, other=0).to(OUT_DT) 

1062 b = tl.load(b_ptr + idx, mask=mask, other=0).to(OUT_DT) 

1063 c = tl.load(c_ptr + idx, mask=mask, other=0).to(OUT_DT) 

1064 tl.store(out_ptr + idx, fn(a, b, c, s.to(OUT_DT)).to(OUT_DT), mask=mask) 

1065 

1066 

1067@triton.jit 

1068def foreach_ternary_kernel( 

1069 meta_ptr, 

1070 scalar_ptr, 

1071 scalar_value: tl.float64, 

1072 fn: tl.constexpr, 

1073 NT: tl.constexpr, 

1074 A_DT: tl.constexpr, 

1075 OUT_DT: tl.constexpr, 

1076 S_DT: tl.constexpr, 

1077 SCALAR_BY_VALUE: tl.constexpr, 

1078 BLOCK: tl.constexpr, 

1079 SWAP: tl.constexpr, 

1080): 

1081 """``NT`` tensors, three tensor inputs and one per-tensor scalar. 

1082 

1083 ``meta_ptr`` layout, all int64:: 

1084 

1085 [0, NT) self pointers 

1086 [NT, 2*NT) tensor1 pointers 

1087 [2*NT, 3*NT) tensor2 pointers 

1088 [3*NT, 4*NT) output pointers 

1089 [4*NT, 5*NT) element counts 

1090 

1091 This serves ``addcmul``/``addcdiv`` (``self + value * t1 <op> t2``) and the 

1092 ``lerp`` weight forms; the scalar array is the ``value``/``weight`` 

1093 argument, broadcast on the host when the overload supplies a single value. 

1094 

1095 ``SCALAR_BY_VALUE`` selects the ``.Scalar`` form: a single value that every 

1096 tensor shares travels as an ordinary kernel argument instead of a device 

1097 buffer. ``scalar_value`` is declared ``float64`` so nothing is lost on the 

1098 way in; the cast to ``S_DT`` reproduces the buffer's rounding exactly. 

1099 

1100 A pointer read out of ``meta_ptr`` carries no alignment information, so 

1101 Triton cannot widen the access and the element-indexed body issues one 

1102 ``ld.global.b16`` per element. ``foreach_ternary_kernel_p4`` already reads 

1103 four 16-bit elements per lane through an ``int64`` pointer, but the caller 

1104 only selects it from ``_PACK_MIN_ELEMS`` upward, so every 512^2 16-bit 

1105 group took the narrow path; that group is where the acceptance median 

1106 lives. Rather than raise the shared threshold, the kernel checks the two 

1107 conditions the packed access needs -- all four pointers 8 byte aligned and 

1108 the count a multiple of four -- on metadata values it has already loaded, 

1109 and inlines the packed body when they hold. Unaligned views and ragged 

1110 counts keep the element-indexed body, so nothing here depends on the 

1111 caller. 

1112 """ 

1113 t = tl.program_id(0) 

1114 a_raw = tl.load(meta_ptr + t) 

1115 b_raw = tl.load(meta_ptr + NT + t) 

1116 c_raw = tl.load(meta_ptr + 2 * NT + t) 

1117 out_raw = tl.load(meta_ptr + 3 * NT + t) 

1118 n_elements = tl.load(meta_ptr + 4 * NT + t) 

1119 

1120 # The packed body splits each loaded word into 16-bit halves, which is only 

1121 # well defined when both the operands and the result are 16 bits wide; for 

1122 # anything else this folds to the narrow body at compile time. 

1123 IS16: tl.constexpr = ( 

1124 (A_DT.primitive_bitwidth == 16) 

1125 & (OUT_DT.primitive_bitwidth == 16) 

1126 & (_PACK_BF16 or A_DT != tl.bfloat16) 

1127 ) 

1128 if IS16: 

1129 if (((a_raw | b_raw | c_raw | out_raw) & 7) == 0) & ((n_elements & 3) == 0): 

1130 foreach_ternary_kernel_p4( 

1131 meta_ptr, 

1132 scalar_ptr, 

1133 scalar_value, 

1134 fn, 

1135 NT, 

1136 A_DT, 

1137 OUT_DT, 

1138 S_DT, 

1139 SCALAR_BY_VALUE, 

1140 BLOCK, 

1141 SWAP, 

1142 ) 

1143 else: 

1144 _ternary_narrow_body( 

1145 a_raw, 

1146 b_raw, 

1147 c_raw, 

1148 out_raw, 

1149 n_elements, 

1150 scalar_ptr, 

1151 scalar_value, 

1152 fn, 

1153 A_DT, 

1154 OUT_DT, 

1155 S_DT, 

1156 SCALAR_BY_VALUE, 

1157 BLOCK, 

1158 SWAP, 

1159 ) 

1160 else: 

1161 _ternary_narrow_body( 

1162 a_raw, 

1163 b_raw, 

1164 c_raw, 

1165 out_raw, 

1166 n_elements, 

1167 scalar_ptr, 

1168 scalar_value, 

1169 fn, 

1170 A_DT, 

1171 OUT_DT, 

1172 S_DT, 

1173 SCALAR_BY_VALUE, 

1174 BLOCK, 

1175 SWAP, 

1176 ) 

1177 

1178 

1179@triton.jit 

1180def foreach_ternary_kernel_p4( 

1181 meta_ptr, 

1182 scalar_ptr, 

1183 scalar_value: tl.float64, 

1184 fn: tl.constexpr, 

1185 NT: tl.constexpr, 

1186 A_DT: tl.constexpr, 

1187 OUT_DT: tl.constexpr, 

1188 S_DT: tl.constexpr, 

1189 SCALAR_BY_VALUE: tl.constexpr, 

1190 BLOCK: tl.constexpr, 

1191 SWAP: tl.constexpr, 

1192): 

1193 """Four 16-bit elements per lane; :func:`foreach_ternary_kernel` semantics. 

1194 

1195 ``SWAP`` puts the tile index on ``program_id(0)`` and the tensor index on 

1196 ``program_id(1)``. The hardware issues blocks in linear program-id order, 

1197 so with the tensor index first the sixteen tiles of one tensor are adjacent 

1198 and the grid walks tensor by tensor; transposed it walks tile by tile, which 

1199 at 1024^2 spreads the live addresses across the list instead of over one 

1200 16 MiB buffer at a time and measured 0.7us less on the 128 MiB ternary 

1201 traffic. Below that size the launch is too short for the difference to 

1202 survive and the transposed order was 0.07us slower at 512^2, so the caller 

1203 enables it only from ``_TERNARY_SWAP_MIN_ELEMS`` up (and only for the 

1204 packed kernel, whose layout this was measured on). 

1205 """ 

1206 if SWAP: 

1207 t = tl.program_id(1) 

1208 offset = tl.program_id(0) * (BLOCK // 4) 

1209 else: 

1210 t = tl.program_id(0) 

1211 offset = tl.program_id(1) * (BLOCK // 4) 

1212 

1213 a_ptr = tl.load(meta_ptr + t).to(tl.pointer_type(tl.int64)) 

1214 b_ptr = tl.load(meta_ptr + NT + t).to(tl.pointer_type(tl.int64)) 

1215 c_ptr = tl.load(meta_ptr + 2 * NT + t).to(tl.pointer_type(tl.int64)) 

1216 out_ptr = tl.load(meta_ptr + 3 * NT + t).to(tl.pointer_type(tl.int64)) 

1217 n_elements = tl.load(meta_ptr + 4 * NT + t) 

1218 if SCALAR_BY_VALUE: 

1219 s = scalar_value.to(S_DT) 

1220 else: 

1221 s = tl.load(scalar_ptr + t) 

1222 s = s.to(OUT_DT) 

1223 

1224 idx = offset + tl.arange(0, BLOCK // 4) 

1225 mask = idx < n_elements // 4 

1226 a0, a1, a2, a3 = _unpack4(tl.load(a_ptr + idx, mask=mask, other=0), A_DT) 

1227 b0, b1, b2, b3 = _unpack4(tl.load(b_ptr + idx, mask=mask, other=0), A_DT) 

1228 c0, c1, c2, c3 = _unpack4(tl.load(c_ptr + idx, mask=mask, other=0), A_DT) 

1229 tl.store( 

1230 out_ptr + idx, 

1231 _pack4( 

1232 fn(a0.to(OUT_DT), b0.to(OUT_DT), c0.to(OUT_DT), s).to(OUT_DT), 

1233 fn(a1.to(OUT_DT), b1.to(OUT_DT), c1.to(OUT_DT), s).to(OUT_DT), 

1234 fn(a2.to(OUT_DT), b2.to(OUT_DT), c2.to(OUT_DT), s).to(OUT_DT), 

1235 fn(a3.to(OUT_DT), b3.to(OUT_DT), c3.to(OUT_DT), s).to(OUT_DT), 

1236 ), 

1237 mask=mask, 

1238 ) 

1239 

1240 

1241# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- 

1242# launch accounting (used by the launch-count regression test) 

1243# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- 

1244 

1245 

1246class _LaunchStats: 

1247 """Counters describing how the last call was decomposed. 

1248 

1249 Kept as plain integers so a test can assert that executor launches track 

1250 the number of ``(device, dtype)`` groups instead of ``len(tensors)``. 

1251 """ 

1252 

1253 def __init__(self) -> None: 

1254 self.reset() 

1255 

1256 def reset(self) -> None: 

1257 self.executor_launches = 0 

1258 self.groups = 0 

1259 self.staged_inputs = 0 

1260 self.writebacks = 0 

1261 

1262 def as_dict(self) -> Dict[str, int]: 

1263 return { 

1264 "executor_launches": self.executor_launches, 

1265 "groups": self.groups, 

1266 "staged_inputs": self.staged_inputs, 

1267 "writebacks": self.writebacks, 

1268 } 

1269 

1270 

1271_STATS = _LaunchStats() 

1272 

1273 

1274def launch_stats() -> Dict[str, int]: 

1275 """Snapshot of the counters from the most recent foreach call.""" 

1276 return _STATS.as_dict() 

1277 

1278 

1279# Every argument of the executor kernels other than the metadata pointer is a 

1280# ``tl.constexpr``, so ``(kernel, NT, fn, dtype, dtype, BLOCK)`` identifies the 

1281# compiled variant exactly and a replay only has to hand the same values to the 

1282# kernel's launcher. Triton's Python dispatch between that lookup and the 

1283# actual launch -- binder, cache-key hash, launch-metadata and hook checks -- 

1284# measured ~4us per launch, about a tenth of the small-shape budget, and none of 

1285# it can change the result. The hit rate is high by construction: a benchmark 

1286# loop launches the same variant thousands of times. 

1287# 

1288# Only the *launcher* is cached. The metadata tensor is built by 

1289# ``_device_meta``, which memoises it per exact value list and stream (see the 

1290# comment there); the kernel only reads it, so a repeat call with the same 

1291# pointers gets the same bytes. 

1292# 

1293# The only thing Triton specializes on here is the metadata pointer's 16-byte 

1294# alignment, so that bit is part of the key and an unusually aligned allocation 

1295# gets a variant of its own rather than a mismatch. A miss, an installed launch 

1296# hook (proton and other instrumentation install one), or a launcher that raises 

1297# all take the normal path, which fills the cache. 

1298_LAUNCH_CACHE: Dict[Tuple[Any, ...], Tuple[Any, Any, Any]] = {} 

1299 

1300# Replay accounting. ``replay`` counts calls served by the cached launcher, 

1301# ``dispatch`` counts calls that went through Triton's dispatcher (first call 

1302# per key, or a fallback). Together they equal the number of group launches, 

1303# which is what makes a "the cache is write-only" bug visible without a probe. 

1304_LAUNCH_STATS: Dict[str, int] = {"replay": 0, "dispatch": 0} 

1305 

1306# One-hit memo in front of ``_LAUNCH_CACHE``. The key tuple holds a device and 

1307# two Triton dtypes, and building plus hashing it measured 1.1us a call at 

1308# sixteen positions; the identity compares below ask the same question in a 

1309# handful of pointer comparisons. A repeated call shape presents the same metadata tensor object 

1310# (``_device_meta`` hands the cached one back), the same kernel, function and 

1311# constexprs, and the same grid, so every field of the dict key is covered: 

1312# ``kernel``, ``nt``, ``fn``, both dtypes, ``block`` and ``grid`` are compared 

1313# directly, and ``meta.device`` plus the alignment bit follow from ``meta is 

1314# last[0]`` (a tensor's device never changes and the bit is a property of its 

1315# ``data_ptr``). The element at index 8 is a replay closure that captures the 

1316# launcher and reads the stream per call. 

1317# 

1318# The entry is only ever the launcher for a key that already replayed 

1319# successfully, and a memo miss falls through to the dict, which is still the 

1320# authority. A dispatch clears it, since Triton may have replaced the compiled 

1321# entry. 

1322_LAST_UNARY_REPLAY: List[Any] = [None] 

1323 

1324 

1325def launch_cache_stats() -> Dict[str, int]: 

1326 """Cumulative hits/misses of the executor launch cache (diagnostics only). 

1327 

1328 Deliberately separate from :func:`launch_stats`, which is a per-call 

1329 snapshot used by the tests. 

1330 """ 

1331 return dict(_LAUNCH_STATS) 

1332 

1333 

1334def _bind_executor_launcher( 

1335 entry: Tuple[Any, Any, Any], 

1336 grid: Tuple[int, int], 

1337 nt: int, 

1338 meta: torch.Tensor, 

1339 fn: Callable, 

1340 dt_in: Any, 

1341 dt_out: Any, 

1342 block: int, 

1343) -> Callable[[], None]: 

1344 """Bind a cached launcher into a zero-argument replay closure. 

1345 

1346 The closure cells are read instead of indexing a tuple on every call, and 

1347 the stream is deliberately *not* captured: ``get_current_stream`` is read 

1348 at launch time so a replay issued under a different ``torch.cuda.stream`` 

1349 still lands on the current stream. 

1350 

1351 ``CudaLauncher.__call__`` does two ``allocate_scratch`` calls and two 

1352 attribute reads before forwarding its ``*args`` to ``self.launch``. When 

1353 there is nothing to allocate and ``self.launch`` is the bare C function -- 

1354 true for every executor kernel, whose signature has no ``tensordesc`` 

1355 entry -- calling it with the full positional list skips that wrapper, which 

1356 measured 0.58us of the 4.3us replay at sixteen positions. Anything else 

1357 takes the public call, exactly as before. 

1358 """ 

1359 launcher, function, packed = entry 

1360 idx = meta.device.index 

1361 g0, g1 = grid 

1362 raw = launcher.launch 

1363 if ( 

1364 isinstance(raw, BuiltinFunctionType) 

1365 and launcher.global_scratch_size == 0 

1366 and launcher.profile_scratch_size == 0 

1367 ): 

1368 coop = launcher.launch_cooperative_grid 

1369 pdl = launcher.launch_pdl 

1370 

1371 def replay() -> None: 

1372 raw( 

1373 g0, 

1374 g1, 

1375 1, 

1376 _triton_driver.active.get_current_stream(idx), 

1377 function, 

1378 coop, 

1379 pdl, 

1380 None, 

1381 None, 

1382 packed, 

1383 None, 

1384 None, 

1385 None, 

1386 meta, 

1387 fn, 

1388 nt, 

1389 dt_in, 

1390 dt_out, 

1391 block, 

1392 ) 

1393 

1394 return replay 

1395 

1396 def replay() -> None: 

1397 launcher( 

1398 g0, 

1399 g1, 

1400 1, 

1401 _triton_driver.active.get_current_stream(idx), 

1402 function, 

1403 packed, 

1404 None, 

1405 None, 

1406 None, 

1407 meta, 

1408 fn, 

1409 nt, 

1410 dt_in, 

1411 dt_out, 

1412 block, 

1413 ) 

1414 

1415 return replay 

1416 

1417 

1418def _launch_executor_kernel( 

1419 kernel: Callable, 

1420 grid: Tuple[int, int], 

1421 nt: int, 

1422 meta: torch.Tensor, 

1423 fn: Callable, 

1424 dt_in: Any, 

1425 dt_out: Any, 

1426 block: int, 

1427) -> None: 

1428 last = _LAST_UNARY_REPLAY[0] 

1429 if ( 

1430 last is not None 

1431 and last[0] is meta 

1432 and last[1] is kernel 

1433 and last[2] == nt 

1434 and last[3] is fn 

1435 and last[4] is dt_in 

1436 and last[5] is dt_out 

1437 and last[6] == block 

1438 and last[7] == grid 

1439 and _hooks_absent() 

1440 ): 

1441 try: 

1442 last[8]() 

1443 except Exception: 

1444 # Fall through: the dict path below retries once, then dispatches. 

1445 _LAST_UNARY_REPLAY[0] = None 

1446 else: 

1447 _LAUNCH_STATS["replay"] += 1 

1448 return 

1449 # ``meta.device`` is part of the key: a compiled kernel belongs to one 

1450 # device's module, so replaying device A's launcher for device B would use 

1451 # the wrong context. 

1452 key = ( 

1453 kernel, 

1454 meta.device, 

1455 nt, 

1456 fn, 

1457 dt_in, 

1458 dt_out, 

1459 block, 

1460 not (meta.data_ptr() & 15), 

1461 ) 

1462 entry = _LAUNCH_CACHE.get(key) 

1463 # ``launch_enter_hook`` is a ``HookChain`` in triton 3.6, never ``None``: 

1464 # the chain exists whether or not anyone subscribed. ``.calls`` is the 

1465 # list of registered callbacks, so an empty list is the real "no hooks" 

1466 # state. Proton and other instrumentation add to it, and a replay would 

1467 # then skip their notifications. 

1468 if entry is not None and _hooks_absent(): 

1469 # Binding is inside the ``try`` as well: a Triton build whose launcher 

1470 # has no ``launch_pdl`` or a different raw signature raises here, and 

1471 # that must fall back to dispatch like any other unusable entry rather 

1472 # than fail every call after the first. 

1473 try: 

1474 replay = _bind_executor_launcher( 

1475 entry, grid, nt, meta, fn, dt_in, dt_out, block 

1476 ) 

1477 replay() 

1478 except Exception: 

1479 # A launcher that cannot be replayed this way is not a correctness 

1480 # problem: forget the entry and let Triton dispatch as usual. 

1481 _LAUNCH_CACHE.pop(key, None) 

1482 else: 

1483 _LAST_UNARY_REPLAY[0] = ( 

1484 meta, 

1485 kernel, 

1486 nt, 

1487 fn, 

1488 dt_in, 

1489 dt_out, 

1490 block, 

1491 grid, 

1492 replay, 

1493 ) 

1494 _LAUNCH_STATS["replay"] += 1 

1495 return 

1496 _LAUNCH_STATS["dispatch"] += 1 

1497 compiled = kernel[grid](meta, fn, nt, dt_in, dt_out, block) 

1498 if compiled is not None: 

1499 # A dispatch may have replaced the compiled entry, so a closure bound to 

1500 # the previous one is no longer known to be current. 

1501 _LAST_UNARY_REPLAY[0] = None 

1502 _LAUNCH_CACHE[key] = ( 

1503 compiled.run, 

1504 compiled.function, 

1505 compiled.packed_metadata, 

1506 ) 

1507 

1508 

1509# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- 

1510# public entry point 

1511# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- 

1512 

1513 

1514# Bound-method handles for the per-tensor walks. ``[NUMEL(t) for t in xs]`` 

1515# binds the method once instead of doing an attribute lookup on every tensor: 

1516# measured 7.8us -> 7.3us over 128 tensors, and the same 0.13us at length 1. 

1517# (``list(map(NUMEL, xs))`` is better still at 128 but costs 0.06us more at 

1518# length 1, and the length-1 rows are the ones with the least to spare.) 

1519_NUMEL = torch.Tensor.numel 

1520_DATA_PTR = torch.Tensor.data_ptr 

1521 

1522 

1523def _launch_group( 

1524 srcs: List[torch.Tensor], 

1525 dsts: List[torch.Tensor], 

1526 fn: Callable, 

1527 in_dtype: torch.dtype, 

1528 device: Any, 

1529 is_complex: bool, 

1530) -> None: 

1531 numels = [_NUMEL(t) for t in srcs] 

1532 max_numel = max(numels) 

1533 if max_numel == 0: 

1534 return 

1535 block = _pick_block(numels) 

1536 

1537 nt = len(srcs) 

1538 # One flat Python list -> one tensor -> one H2D transfer. Building this as 

1539 # three separate tensors and slicing them in measured noticeably slower, 

1540 # because each slice assignment is its own copy. 

1541 # 

1542 # An in-place call passes the same list object as both sources and 

1543 # destinations, so the pointer run is read once instead of twice. 

1544 # 

1545 # A pinned staging pool was tried here and rejected. In isolation the pinned 

1546 # copy is 1.7-3.8x faster than this pageable one, but reusing pinned buffers 

1547 # without ordering the host refill against the outstanding device read is a 

1548 # real data race (a probe that forced the window open corrupted 21 of 24 

1549 # calls). Making it safe needs a CUDA event per call, and allocating plus 

1550 # recording that event costs more than the pageable copy saves: end to end it 

1551 # measured 93us per call against 46us for this version. 

1552 ptrs = [_DATA_PTR(t) for t in srcs] 

1553 if dsts is srcs: 

1554 values = ptrs + ptrs + numels 

1555 else: 

1556 values = ptrs + [_DATA_PTR(t) for t in dsts] + numels 

1557 meta = _device_meta(values, device) 

1558 

1559 # ``triton.cdiv`` is a decorated helper and costs ~0.9us at this size; 

1560 # plain ints give the same ceiling division. 

1561 grid = (nt, -(-max_numel // block)) 

1562 if is_complex: 

1563 real_dtype = _COMPLEX_TO_REAL[in_dtype] 

1564 acc = tl.float32 if real_dtype is not torch.float64 else tl.float64 

1565 kernel = ( 

1566 foreach_unary_c2r_kernel 

1567 if dsts[0].dtype.is_floating_point 

1568 else foreach_unary_c2c_kernel 

1569 ) 

1570 _launch_executor_kernel( 

1571 kernel, grid, nt, meta, fn, tl_dtype(real_dtype), acc, block 

1572 ) 

1573 else: 

1574 kernel = ( 

1575 foreach_unary_kernel_p4 

1576 if _pack_ok((in_dtype, dsts[0].dtype), max_numel, values) 

1577 else foreach_unary_kernel 

1578 ) 

1579 _launch_executor_kernel( 

1580 kernel, 

1581 grid, 

1582 nt, 

1583 meta, 

1584 fn, 

1585 tl_dtype(in_dtype), 

1586 tl_dtype(dsts[0].dtype), 

1587 block, 

1588 ) 

1589 _STATS.executor_launches += 1 

1590 _STATS.groups += 1 

1591 

1592 

1593def check_dtype_supported( 

1594 dtype: torch.dtype, 

1595 allowed: Optional[frozenset], 

1596 message: Optional[str] = None, 

1597 error_type: type = RuntimeError, 

1598) -> None: 

1599 """Reject dtypes the corresponding ATen operator also rejects. 

1600 

1601 ``allowed=None`` means "no restriction". Each operator's set was measured 

1602 against this PyTorch build rather than assumed, because the exclusions are 

1603 not guessable: ``_foreach_floor`` rejects ``bool`` but accepts every integer 

1604 dtype, ``_foreach_frac`` rejects all integers, and ``_foreach_sign`` 

1605 accepts ``bool`` while rejecting complex. 

1606 

1607 ``message`` overrides the generic text for operators whose ATen refusal is 

1608 worded differently, such as ``sub`` on bool. ``error_type`` matches the 

1609 class ATen raises, which for ``pow`` on bool is ``NotImplementedError``. 

1610 """ 

1611 if allowed is not None and dtype not in allowed: 

1612 if message is not None: 

1613 raise error_type(message) 

1614 raise error_type( 

1615 f'"foreach" not implemented for \'{str(dtype).replace("torch.", "")}\'' 

1616 ) 

1617 

1618 

1619# ``flag_gems`` overrides ``Tensor.copy_`` on the CUDA key inside 

1620# ``use_gems()``, and ``_device_meta`` runs that copy once per group. The gems 

1621# wrapper validates its arguments and then re-dispatches this CPU->CUDA copy to 

1622# the composite aten kernel anyway, so address that implementation directly. 

1623# The handle is optional: a build without ``redispatch`` keeps the method. 

1624try: 

1625 _ATEN_COMPOSITE_KEYSET = torch._C.DispatchKeySet( 

1626 torch._C.DispatchKey.CompositeExplicitAutograd 

1627 ) 

1628except (AttributeError, RuntimeError): # pragma: no cover - depends on torch build 

1629 _ATEN_COMPOSITE_KEYSET = None 

1630 

1631try: 

1632 _ATEN_COPY_REDISPATCH = torch.ops.aten.copy_.default.redispatch 

1633except (AttributeError, RuntimeError): # pragma: no cover - depends on torch build 

1634 _ATEN_COPY_REDISPATCH = None 

1635 

1636 

1637def foreach_unary( 

1638 tensors: Sequence[torch.Tensor], 

1639 fn: Callable, 

1640 *, 

1641 complex_fn: Optional[Callable] = None, 

1642 out_dtype_fn: Callable[[torch.dtype], torch.dtype] = same_dtype, 

1643 inplace: bool = False, 

1644 allowed_dtypes: Optional[frozenset] = None, 

1645) -> List[torch.Tensor]: 

1646 """Apply a unary elementwise ``triton.jit`` function to a whole TensorList. 

1647 

1648 Args: 

1649 tensors: the ``Tensor[]`` argument as received from ATen. 

1650 fn: ``@triton.jit`` function of one value, used for real dtypes. 

1651 complex_fn: ``@triton.jit`` function of ``(re, im)`` for complex 

1652 inputs. ``None`` means complex is unsupported by this operator. 

1653 out_dtype_fn: maps input dtype to output dtype. 

1654 inplace: write results back into ``tensors`` and return them. 

1655 allowed_dtypes: dtypes the operator accepts; ``None`` means all. 

1656 

1657 Returns: 

1658 A list of result tensors, one per input, in input order. 

1659 """ 

1660 tensors = check_tensor_list(tensors) 

1661 _STATS.reset() 

1662 

1663 # Fast path: one device, one dtype. Bucketing exists for the mixed case, 

1664 # and its dict/tuple bookkeeping is the largest per-tensor cost in this 

1665 # walk; every unary operator here is normally called that way, so pay for 

1666 # the general machinery only when the list actually mixes. 

1667 first = tensors[0] 

1668 device = first.device 

1669 dtype = first.dtype 

1670 if allowed_dtypes is not None and dtype not in allowed_dtypes: 

1671 check_dtype_supported(dtype, allowed_dtypes) 

1672 if dtype.is_complex and complex_fn is None: 

1673 raise NotImplementedError(f"foreach executor has no complex kernel for {dtype}") 

1674 out_dtype = out_dtype_fn(dtype) 

1675 if inplace and out_dtype != dtype: 

1676 # Same refusal as ATen: an in-place op may not silently narrow its 

1677 # promoted result back into the input's dtype. 

1678 raise RuntimeError( 

1679 f"result type {str(out_dtype).replace('torch.', '').capitalize()}" 

1680 " can't be cast to the desired output type " 

1681 f"{str(dtype).replace('torch.', '').capitalize()}" 

1682 ) 

1683 is_complex = dtype.is_complex 

1684 kernel_fn = complex_fn if is_complex else fn 

1685 

1686 # Bulk path: one device, one dtype, every input flat-addressable, real dtypes. 

1687 # ATen's C++ grouping primitive answers the device/dtype question for the 

1688 # whole list in one call -- measured 9.9us against 16.6us for the per-tensor 

1689 # attribute walk over 128 tensors -- and ``map`` allocates the outputs 

1690 # without any per-tensor loop bookkeeping. Paired against the unchanged 

1691 # module (interleaved, order-rotated, nine do_bench medians per side) that 

1692 # is 40.9us of a 301.6us call at (64,) x 128, 40.2us at 65536 x 128 and 

1693 # 3.8us at (64,) x 16, and inside the timer quantum at length 1. Mixed lists, gappy inputs that need 

1694 # staging, and complex inputs fall through to the general loop below, which 

1695 # keeps the exact ATen error contract for them: when the grouping call 

1696 # raises or reports more than one group, nothing here has been touched. 

1697 if not is_complex and _GROUP_TENSORS is not None: 

1698 try: 

1699 uniform = len(_GROUP_TENSORS([tensors], False)) == 1 

1700 except Exception: 

1701 uniform = False # let the general loop below produce the error 

1702 # ``is_flat_addressable`` answers the common case on its first line but 

1703 # costs a Python call frame per tensor. Asking that same first line in 

1704 # one C-level ``map`` measured 11.2us -> 6.5us over 128 tensors, and a 

1705 # False just falls through to the full predicate, so the boolean is 

1706 # unchanged. ``_IS_CONTIGUOUS`` is the module-level unbound descriptor 

1707 # defined with the grouping helpers below. 

1708 if uniform and ( 

1709 all(map(_IS_CONTIGUOUS, tensors)) or all(map(is_flat_addressable, tensors)) 

1710 ): 

1711 if inplace: 

1712 # Flat implies non-overlapping and dense, so the overlap probe 

1713 # cannot change the answer and no staging copy is needed. 

1714 _launch_group(tensors, tensors, kernel_fn, dtype, device, False) 

1715 return tensors 

1716 if out_dtype == dtype: 

1717 # One-argument form: it skips the keyword's dispatch work and 

1718 # allocates the identical tensor whenever the output dtype is 

1719 # the input's, which is the float case. 

1720 dsts = list(map(torch.empty_like, tensors)) 

1721 else: 

1722 dsts = [torch.empty_like(t, dtype=out_dtype) for t in tensors] 

1723 _launch_group(tensors, dsts, kernel_fn, dtype, device, False) 

1724 return dsts 

1725 

1726 results: List[torch.Tensor] = [] 

1727 srcs: List[torch.Tensor] = [] 

1728 dsts: List[torch.Tensor] = [] 

1729 writebacks: List[Tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]] = [] 

1730 

1731 for t in tensors: 

1732 if t.dtype != dtype or t.device != device: 

1733 # Mixed list: redo the call through the bucketing path. The 

1734 # counters are reset so staging done above is not counted twice. 

1735 _STATS.reset() 

1736 return _foreach_unary_grouped( 

1737 tensors, 

1738 fn, 

1739 complex_fn=complex_fn, 

1740 out_dtype_fn=out_dtype_fn, 

1741 inplace=inplace, 

1742 allowed_dtypes=allowed_dtypes, 

1743 ) 

1744 flat = is_flat_addressable(t) 

1745 if inplace: 

1746 # A flat-addressable tensor is non-overlapping-and-dense by 

1747 # definition, so the dispatcher-backed probe cannot change the 

1748 # answer there; skipping it saves a dispatch per tensor. 

1749 if not flat and has_internal_overlap(t): 

1750 raise RuntimeError( 

1751 "unsupported operation: more than one element of the " 

1752 "written-to tensor refers to a single memory location. " 

1753 "Please clone() the tensor before performing the operation." 

1754 ) 

1755 if flat: 

1756 src = t 

1757 else: 

1758 # Gappy view: compute on a dense copy, then scatter back. 

1759 src = t.contiguous() 

1760 writebacks.append((t, src)) 

1761 _STATS.staged_inputs += 1 

1762 results.append(t) 

1763 else: 

1764 src = t if flat else t.contiguous() 

1765 if src is not t: 

1766 _STATS.staged_inputs += 1 

1767 # empty_like reproduces PyTorch's foreach output stride policy: it 

1768 # keeps a dense tensor's stride (so transposed inputs give 

1769 # transposed outputs) and normalizes everything else to contiguous. 

1770 # One allocation per tensor, not one packed buffer plus unbind, is 

1771 # also what keeps aliasing observable-equivalent to ATen: no two 

1772 # outputs of a call share a storage (checked on two 4x4, 

1773 # mixed-shape, transposed, zero-dim and one-element lists). 

1774 if out_dtype == src.dtype: 

1775 # The one-argument form is measurably cheaper (it skips the 

1776 # keyword's dispatch work) and allocates the identical tensor 

1777 # when the output dtype is the input's -- the float case. 

1778 dst = torch.empty_like(src) 

1779 else: 

1780 dst = torch.empty_like(src, dtype=out_dtype) 

1781 results.append(dst) 

1782 dsts.append(dst) 

1783 srcs.append(src) 

1784 

1785 if inplace: 

1786 # Same list object: ``_launch_group`` then knows the pointers occur 

1787 # twice in a row and reads each ``data_ptr`` once. Returning the 

1788 # inputs themselves means the only aliasing is what the caller passed 

1789 # in (a tensor repeated twice stays shared), as with ATen. 

1790 dsts = srcs 

1791 _launch_group(srcs, dsts, kernel_fn, dtype, device, is_complex) 

1792 

1793 for dst_view, staged in writebacks: 

1794 dst_view.copy_(staged) 

1795 _STATS.writebacks += 1 

1796 

1797 return results 

1798 

1799 

1800def _foreach_unary_grouped( 

1801 tensors: Sequence[torch.Tensor], 

1802 fn: Callable, 

1803 *, 

1804 complex_fn: Optional[Callable] = None, 

1805 out_dtype_fn: Callable[[torch.dtype], torch.dtype] = same_dtype, 

1806 inplace: bool = False, 

1807 allowed_dtypes: Optional[frozenset] = None, 

1808) -> List[torch.Tensor]: 

1809 """Bucketing path for a TensorList that mixes devices or dtypes. 

1810 

1811 ``tensors`` is already validated and normalised to a list. 

1812 """ 

1813 results: List[Optional[torch.Tensor]] = [None] * len(tensors) 

1814 # Buckets keyed by (device, input dtype); values are aligned src/dst lists. 

1815 buckets: Dict[Tuple[Any, torch.dtype], Tuple[List, List]] = {} 

1816 writebacks: List[Tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]] = [] 

1817 

1818 for i, t in enumerate(tensors): 

1819 dtype = t.dtype 

1820 # The helper is only a message builder; calling it per tensor for the 

1821 # accepted case measured 0.6us on a sixteen-tensor list. 

1822 if allowed_dtypes is not None and dtype not in allowed_dtypes: 

1823 check_dtype_supported(dtype, allowed_dtypes) 

1824 if dtype.is_complex and complex_fn is None: 

1825 raise NotImplementedError( 

1826 f"foreach executor has no complex kernel for {dtype}" 

1827 ) 

1828 out_dtype = out_dtype_fn(dtype) 

1829 key = (t.device, dtype) 

1830 flat = is_flat_addressable(t) 

1831 

1832 if inplace: 

1833 if out_dtype != dtype: 

1834 # Same refusal as ATen: an in-place op may not silently narrow 

1835 # its promoted result back into the input's dtype. 

1836 raise RuntimeError( 

1837 f"result type {str(out_dtype).replace('torch.', '').capitalize()}" 

1838 " can't be cast to the desired output type " 

1839 f"{str(dtype).replace('torch.', '').capitalize()}" 

1840 ) 

1841 # A flat-addressable tensor is non-overlapping-and-dense by 

1842 # definition, so the dispatcher-backed probe cannot change the 

1843 # answer there; skipping it saves a dispatch per tensor. 

1844 if not flat and has_internal_overlap(t): 

1845 raise RuntimeError( 

1846 "unsupported operation: more than one element of the " 

1847 "written-to tensor refers to a single memory location. " 

1848 "Please clone() the tensor before performing the operation." 

1849 ) 

1850 if flat: 

1851 src = dst = t 

1852 else: 

1853 # Gappy view: compute on a dense copy, then scatter back. 

1854 src = dst = t.contiguous() 

1855 writebacks.append((t, src)) 

1856 _STATS.staged_inputs += 1 

1857 results[i] = t 

1858 else: 

1859 src = t if flat else t.contiguous() 

1860 if src is not t: 

1861 _STATS.staged_inputs += 1 

1862 # empty_like reproduces PyTorch's foreach output stride policy: it 

1863 # keeps a dense tensor's stride (so transposed inputs give 

1864 # transposed outputs) and normalizes everything else to contiguous. 

1865 if out_dtype == src.dtype: 

1866 # The one-argument form is measurably cheaper (it skips the 

1867 # keyword's dispatch work) and allocates the identical tensor 

1868 # when the output dtype is the input's -- the float case. 

1869 dst = torch.empty_like(src) 

1870 else: 

1871 dst = torch.empty_like(src, dtype=out_dtype) 

1872 results[i] = dst 

1873 

1874 bucket = buckets.get(key) 

1875 if bucket is None: 

1876 bucket = buckets[key] = ([], []) 

1877 bucket[0].append(src) 

1878 bucket[1].append(dst) 

1879 

1880 for (device, dtype), (srcs, dsts) in buckets.items(): 

1881 kernel_fn = complex_fn if dtype.is_complex else fn 

1882 _launch_group(srcs, dsts, kernel_fn, dtype, device, dtype.is_complex) 

1883 

1884 for dst_view, staged in writebacks: 

1885 dst_view.copy_(staged) 

1886 _STATS.writebacks += 1 

1887 

1888 return results # type: ignore[return-value] 

1889 

1890 

1891# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- 

1892# multi-input entry points 

1893# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- 

1894 

1895 

1896def _dense(t: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor: 

1897 """A flat-addressable view of ``t``, copying only when necessary. 

1898 

1899 Unlike the unary path, a merely *dense* tensor is not enough for the paired 

1900 kernels: two tensors that are each dense but carry different strides would 

1901 be matched up element-by-element in the wrong order under flat indexing. 

1902 ``contiguous()`` is therefore the condition here, not 

1903 ``is_non_overlapping_and_dense``. 

1904 """ 

1905 if t.is_contiguous(): 

1906 return t 

1907 _STATS.staged_inputs += 1 

1908 return t.contiguous() 

1909 

1910 

1911def _check_same_length(a: Sequence[torch.Tensor], b: Sequence[Any], what: str) -> None: 

1912 if len(a) != len(b): 

1913 raise RuntimeError( 

1914 f"Tensor list must have same number of elements as {what}, " 

1915 f"got {len(a)} and {len(b)}" 

1916 ) 

1917 

1918 

1919def _result_dtype(t: torch.Tensor, other: Any) -> torch.dtype: 

1920 """ATen's type promotion for one tensor against a tensor or a number. 

1921 

1922 Delegating to ``torch.result_type`` rather than reimplementing the lattice 

1923 is deliberate: it is the same routine ATen consults, so an int64 list plus a 

1924 float scalar promotes to float32 here exactly as ``torch._foreach_add`` 

1925 does. 

1926 """ 

1927 return torch.result_type(t, other) 

1928 

1929 

1930# Promotion is a pure function of the operand dtypes (plus whether an operand is 

1931# zero-dimensional, which ATen treats as a weak scalar), so the answer is 

1932# memoised: a 16-tensor list asks the same question 16 times. 

1933_PROMOTION_CACHE: Dict[Tuple[Any, ...], torch.dtype] = {} 

1934 

1935 

1936def _promotion_probe(t: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor: 

1937 """A meta tensor standing in for ``t`` in a ``result_type`` query.""" 

1938 if t.dim() == 0: 

1939 return torch.empty((), dtype=t.dtype, device="meta") 

1940 return torch.empty(0, dtype=t.dtype, device="meta") 

1941 

1942 

1943def _promote_dtypes( 

1944 a: torch.Tensor, b: torch.Tensor, c: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None 

1945) -> torch.dtype: 

1946 """Two- or three-way ``result_type`` fold, memoised on the operand shapes. 

1947 

1948 ``result_type`` takes two operands, so a three-way promotion is a fold with 

1949 an intermediate dtype. The original spelled that intermediate out as a 

1950 fresh ``meta`` tensor per tensor in the list, which measured 54us for a 

1951 16-tensor ``addcmul`` -- more than the kernel it feeds. Nothing about the 

1952 answer depends on the values, so the dtype tuple keys a dict instead. 

1953 """ 

1954 key = ( 

1955 a.dtype, 

1956 a.dim() == 0, 

1957 b.dtype, 

1958 b.dim() == 0, 

1959 c.dtype if c is not None else None, 

1960 c is not None and c.dim() == 0, 

1961 ) 

1962 out = _PROMOTION_CACHE.get(key) 

1963 if out is None: 

1964 out = torch.result_type(_promotion_probe(a), _promotion_probe(b)) 

1965 if c is not None: 

1966 out = torch.result_type( 

1967 torch.empty(0, dtype=out, device="meta"), _promotion_probe(c) 

1968 ) 

1969 _PROMOTION_CACHE[key] = out 

1970 return out 

1971 

1972 

1973def _promote_with_scalar(dtype: torch.dtype, value: Any) -> torch.dtype: 

1974 """``result_type(tensor, scalar)`` memoised on ``(dtype, type(value))``. 

1975 

1976 A Python number is a weak scalar, so its *value* never changes the answer -- 

1977 only its type (an ``int`` keeps an integral tensor integral, a ``float`` 

1978 promotes it to the default float dtype). A zero-dimensional tensor is also 

1979 weak, so the probe only has to match that one property. 

1980 """ 

1981 zero_dim = isinstance(value, torch.Tensor) and value.dim() == 0 

1982 key = ("scalar", dtype, type(value), zero_dim) 

1983 out = _PROMOTION_CACHE.get(key) 

1984 if out is None: 

1985 probe = torch.empty(0, dtype=dtype, device="meta") 

1986 out = torch.result_type(probe, value) 

1987 _PROMOTION_CACHE[key] = out 

1988 return out 

1989 

1990 

1991def _common_scalar(vals: Sequence[Any]) -> Optional[Any]: 

1992 """The single value every slot shares, or ``None`` when they differ. 

1993 

1994 ``==`` on its own would fold ``0.0`` and ``-0.0`` together; the sign bit 

1995 matters because ``div``/``pow`` turn it into ``+inf`` versus ``-inf``. 

1996 NaNs never compare equal, so they fall through to the per-tensor buffer. 

1997 """ 

1998 # ``float`` is what the device-buffer path would have applied anyway, and 

1999 # it keeps the by-value argument a plain number even if a caller handed in 

2000 # zero-dimensional tensors. 

2001 first = float(vals[0]) 

2002 if first == 0.0: 

2003 sign = math.copysign(1.0, first) 

2004 for v in vals: 

2005 v = float(v) 

2006 if v != first or math.copysign(1.0, v) != sign: 

2007 return None 

2008 return first 

2009 # Outside the zeros the value itself carries the sign, so the explicit 

2010 # sign-bit test is only needed for ±0.0. ``count`` is the same equality 

2011 # scan driven from C: it measured 0.06us against 0.49us for the Python loop 

2012 # over the sixteen entries of a ``.ScalarList`` call. 

2013 count = getattr(vals, "count", None) 

2014 if count is None: # pragma: no cover - every call site passes a list 

2015 for v in vals: 

2016 if float(v) != first: 

2017 return None 

2018 return first 

2019 return first if count(first) == len(vals) else None 

2020 

2021 

2022def _meta_from_values(values: List[int], device: Any) -> torch.Tensor: 

2023 """Build an int64 device tensor holding ``values`` (one pageable H2D copy). 

2024 

2025 ``array.array`` + ``frombuffer`` skips the generic sequence-to-tensor path, 

2026 and going through ``empty`` + ``copy_`` sidesteps the dispatcher's 

2027 ``_to_copy``: inside ``use_gems()`` the plain ``torch.tensor(...).to(device)`` 

2028 form runs the gems implementation and measured 21.5us against 13.1us here. 

2029 

2030 The copy addresses the composite aten implementation directly. Inside 

2031 ``use_gems()`` the ``Tensor.copy_`` method runs flag_gems' Python wrapper, 

2032 which validates its arguments and then redispatches this CPU->CUDA copy to 

2033 exactly that composite kernel anyway; the wrapper measured ~10us per call 

2034 (P1's cProfile: ``copy_`` cumulative 13.5-14.9us, of which the transfer is 

2035 small). ``redispatch`` is only an optimisation, so a build without it falls 

2036 back to the regular method. 

2037 """ 

2038 host = torch.frombuffer(array.array("q", values), dtype=torch.int64) 

2039 out = torch.empty(len(values), dtype=torch.int64, device=device) 

2040 if ( 

2041 _ATEN_COPY_REDISPATCH is None 

2042 or _ATEN_COMPOSITE_KEYSET is None 

2043 or out.device.type == "npu" 

2044 ): 

2045 # Ascend NPU registers aten::_copy_from under PrivateUse1, not under 

2046 # CompositeExplicitAutograd. Redispatching at CompositeExplicitAutograd 

2047 # skips that key and raises NotImplementedError on NPU; use the regular 

2048 # copy_ path instead, which routes through the full dispatch stack. 

2049 out.copy_(host, non_blocking=True) 

2050 else: 

2051 # Skip the Python-level copy_ registration and go straight to the 

2052 # CompositeExplicitAutograd implementation. 

2053 _ATEN_COPY_REDISPATCH(_ATEN_COMPOSITE_KEYSET, out, host, True) 

2054 return out 

2055 

2056 

2057# A pageable H2D copy blocks the host until the stream reaches it, and it is the 

2058# single largest exposed cost of a small foreach call: the request is 100-200 

2059# bytes wide, so the transfer itself is nothing and the wait is everything. 

2060# In a steady loop the request is byte-identical from call to call -- the same 

2061# tensor list, and outputs served from the caching allocator's recycled blocks 

2062# -- so the built tensor can be reused instead of rebuilt. 

2063# 

2064# Reuse is exact, not a heuristic about what the metadata "probably" is: the key 

2065# is the whole value list, so a hit can only return a buffer whose contents are 

2066# the bytes this call would have written. The buffer is never written again 

2067# after it is built and the kernel only reads it, so an in-flight launch from an 

2068# earlier call cannot observe anything different. The *stream* is part of the 

2069# key because that ordering argument is per stream: a buffer built on stream A 

2070# is only picked up by calls that run on stream A, where the H2D that produced 

2071# it is ordered before the new launch. A call on another stream simply misses 

2072# and builds its own. Nothing is refilled, so this does not reintroduce the 

2073# reuse hazard that sank the pinned staging pool (that pool rewrote the bytes a 

2074# DMA was still reading). 

2075# 

2076# The bound keeps a workload whose addresses keep moving from growing the cache 

2077# without limit; insertion order is the eviction order. 

2078_META_CACHE: Dict[Tuple[Any, int, Tuple[int, ...]], torch.Tensor] = {} 

2079_META_CACHE_LIMIT = 32 

2080 

2081# Last-hit shortcut in front of the memo above. Building the key (``tuple``
