2082# over the 4*16 entries plus its hash) measured 1.07us, while the same 

2083# comparison against a retained copy of the previous value list is a single 

2084# C-level list compare at 0.09us -- a steady-state call re-launches with the 

2085# same addresses, because the caching allocator hands back the blocks the 

2086# previous call released. [values, stream, device, buffer] 

2087# 

2088# The copy is made so that a caller which mutates a reused list in place is 

2089# still compared against what was actually uploaded. A tuple needs no copy 

2090# (immutable) and is retained as the caller built it: the ternary launcher 

2091# hands in a freshly built tuple, and comparing it against a stored *list* 

2092# could never be equal, which is what kept this shortcut dead on that path. 

2093_LAST_META: List[Any] = [None, None, None, None] 

2094 

2095 

2096def _device_meta(values: List[int], device: Any) -> torch.Tensor: 

2097 """A read-only int64 device tensor holding ``values`` (memoised). 

2098 

2099 See :func:`_meta_from_values` for how it is built and the cache comment 

2100 above for why a hit is exact. 

2101 """ 

2102 # ``device`` is a ``torch.device`` carrying an index at every call site; a 

2103 # bare ``torch.device("cuda")`` means the current device, which is what 

2104 # ``torch.empty`` would have used. 

2105 index = device.index if isinstance(device, torch.device) else None 

2106 if index is None: 

2107 index = torch.cuda.current_device() 

2108 stream = _triton_driver.active.get_current_stream(index) 

2109 last = _LAST_META 

2110 if last[1] is stream and last[2] == device and last[0] == values: 

2111 return last[3] 

2112 key = (device, stream, tuple(values)) 

2113 cached = _META_CACHE.get(key) 

2114 if cached is None: 

2115 cached = _meta_from_values(values, device) 

2116 if len(_META_CACHE) >= _META_CACHE_LIMIT: 

2117 _META_CACHE.pop(next(iter(_META_CACHE))) 

2118 _META_CACHE[key] = cached 

2119 last[0] = values if isinstance(values, tuple) else list(values) 

2120 last[1] = stream 

2121 last[2] = device 

2122 last[3] = cached 

2123 return cached 

2124 

2125 

2126def _resolve_scalars( 

2127 tensors: Sequence[torch.Tensor], scalars: Any 

2128) -> Tuple[List[Any], Optional[float], Optional[type]]: 

2129 """Normalise the ``.Scalar`` / ``.ScalarList`` / ``.Tensor`` forms into a list. 

2130 

2131 The ``.Tensor`` overloads of ``addcmul``/``addcdiv`` take the values as a 

2132 one-dimensional tensor holding one entry per tensor in the list (ATen 

2133 requires it on the CPU), so it is unpacked here rather than being mistaken 

2134 for a single value. 

2135 

2136 Returns ``(values, common, vclass)``: one entry per tensor, plus the value 

2137 every entry shares as a ``float`` -- or ``None`` when a scan is needed to 

2138 find out, or when the value is not a real number and cannot be converted -- 

2139 plus the Python type of every entry when the broadcast form makes it one 

2140 object repeated (``None`` when it has to be looked at per element). A plain 

2141 broadcast scalar is already its own common value, so the equality scan that 

2142 ``_common_scalar`` performs can be skipped for it. 

2143 

2144 ``float`` conversion is limited to ``numbers.Real`` so that an illegal 

2145 complex scalar keeps the error the base implementation produced: the 

2146 launcher's ``_common_scalar`` raises ``TypeError`` for it, and for an 

2147 all-empty tensor list -- where the launch is skipped -- the call returns 

2148 the promoted empty outputs instead of failing early here. 

2149 """ 

2150 if type(scalars) is float: 

2151 # A plain float is the common form and is already its own common 

2152 # value; reaching the same answer through the three ``isinstance`` 

2153 # tests below (one of them against the ``numbers.Real`` ABC) costs 

2154 # 0.4us a call. 

2155 return [scalars] * len(tensors), scalars, float 

2156 if isinstance(scalars, torch.Tensor): 

2157 if scalars.numel() == 1: 

2158 value = scalars.item() 

2159 # Keep the Python type of the original value in ``values``: an 

2160 # ``int`` scalar promotes an integral tensor differently from a 

2161 # ``float``. The by-value argument is always the float the device 

2162 # buffer would have held. 

2163 if isinstance(value, numbers.Real): 

2164 return [value] * len(tensors), float(value), type(value) 

2165 return [value] * len(tensors), None, None 

2166 _check_same_length(tensors, scalars, "scalar list") 

2167 # ``tolist`` reads the elements; ``detach`` and ``cpu`` only built two 

2168 # throwaway tensors first (the ATen overload already requires CPU, and 

2169 # ``tolist`` syncs on its own if a build ever lets a device tensor 

2170 # through). Measured 2.1us of the call at sixteen entries. 

2171 values = scalars.tolist() 

2172 return values, _common_scalar(values), None 

2173 if isinstance(scalars, (list, tuple)): 

2174 _check_same_length(tensors, scalars, "scalar list") 

2175 # The scored ``.ScalarList`` call hands in ``[0.5] * 16``: an exact 

2176 # ``float`` repeated. ``list.count`` runs the same ``==`` scan 

2177 # ``_common_scalar`` drives from C, so the common value is known 

2178 # without the copy and without the helper -- and ``values`` is only 

2179 # ever read downstream (the general loop, ``_ternary_upload``, 

2180 # ``_common_scalar``), never stored or mutated, so the caller's list 

2181 # can be passed through as it is. Restricted to a ``list`` whose head 

2182 # is an exact ``float``: a tuple keeps its own type, and the ±0.0 sign 

2183 # case still goes through ``_common_scalar``. 

2184 if type(scalars) is list and scalars: 

2185 first = scalars[0] 

2186 if ( 

2187 type(first) is float 

2188 and first != 0.0 

2189 and scalars.count(first) == len(scalars) 

2190 ): 

2191 return scalars, first, None 

2192 values = list(scalars) 

2193 return values, _common_scalar(values), None 

2194 if isinstance(scalars, numbers.Real): 

2195 return [scalars] * len(tensors), float(scalars), type(scalars) 

2196 return [scalars] * len(tensors), None, None 

2197 

2198 

2199def _finish_inplace( 

2200 results: List[torch.Tensor], 

2201 writebacks: List[Tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]], 

2202) -> None: 

2203 for dst_view, staged in writebacks: 

2204 dst_view.copy_(staged) 

2205 _STATS.writebacks += 1 

2206 del results 

2207 

2208 

2209# ATen's own TensorList grouping primitive: one C++ pass over the lists, keyed 

2210# by ``(device, dtype)``. The executor only needs the *number* of groups to 

2211# decide whether a call is uniform, and measured 2.8us against 6.3us for the 

2212# per-tensor attribute walk over two sixteen-tensor lists. Absent on a build 

2213# without it, in which case the walk below is used. 

2214try: 

2215 _GROUP_TENSORS = torch._C._group_tensors_by_device_and_dtype 

2216except AttributeError: # pragma: no cover - very old builds 

2217 _GROUP_TENSORS = None 

2218 

2219 

2220def _binary_homogeneous( 

2221 self: List[torch.Tensor], 

2222 other: List[torch.Tensor], 

2223 fn: Callable, 

2224 inplace: bool, 

2225 alpha: float, 

2226 allowed_dtypes: Optional[frozenset], 

2227 dtype_error: Optional[str], 

2228 dtype_error_type: type, 

2229 out_dtype_fn: Optional[Callable[[torch.dtype], torch.dtype]], 

2230 out_dtypes: Optional[Sequence[torch.dtype]], 

2231 scalar_operand: bool, 

2232) -> Optional[List[torch.Tensor]]: 

2233 """Execute a uniform binary list in one bucket, or return ``None``. 

2234 

2235 ``None`` means the caller's lists need the general per-tensor bucket loop; 

2236 it is the answer for every kind of heterogeneity that loop exists to 

2237 handle (device, dtype, rank class, per-position output dtype). The scan 

2238 that decides this is also the only per-tensor work left on the hot path: 

2239 the list arguments, dtype checks and result allocation are comprehensions. 

2240 

2241 ``scalar_operand`` lists are one repeated single-element tensor by 

2242 contract, so they are neither scanned nor staged: a one-element tensor is 

2243 always contiguous and flat-addressable. 

2244 """ 

2245 a0 = self[0] 

2246 dev = a0.device 

2247 dt_a = a0.dtype 

2248 # When ``out_dtypes`` pins the result the promotion is fixed, so the rank 

2249 # class of an operand can no longer change it and is not checked. 

2250 need_promotion = out_dtypes is None 

2251 b0 = other[0] 

2252 dt_b = b0.dtype 

2253 # Uniform in device *and* dtype is the hot case. One C++ grouping pass 

2254 # answers it for both lists at once, and the alternative -- walking both 

2255 # lists in Python -- was the single largest host cost left here. The 

2256 # comment used to argue the two generator passes won on the strength of a 

2257 # standalone timing of the idiom in isolation; measured in situ inside the 

2258 # scored benchmark (source-exact substitution, 16 tensors), the grouping 

2259 # pass is 1.0-1.7us cheaper on ``_foreach_add.List``. When both lists are 

2260 # uniform the promotion is the identity and the rank class of an operand 

2261 # cannot change the result dtype, so the per-tensor ``dim()`` check below 

2262 # is skipped too. 

2263 # ``scalar_operand`` lists are one repeated single-element tensor, whose 

2264 # dtype may legitimately differ from ``self``'s, so they keep the walk. 

2265 uniform = False 

2266 if not scalar_operand and dt_b is dt_a: 

2267 if _GROUP_TENSORS is not None: 

2268 uniform = len(_GROUP_TENSORS([self + other], False)) == 1 

2269 else: 

2270 uniform = all(t.dtype is dt_a and t.device == dev for t in self) and all( 

2271 t.dtype is dt_a and t.device == dev for t in other 

2272 ) 

2273 if not uniform: 

2274 zero_dim = a0.dim() == 0 

2275 for t in self: 

2276 if t.dtype is not dt_a or t.device != dev: 

2277 return None 

2278 if need_promotion and (t.dim() == 0) != zero_dim: 

2279 return None 

2280 

2281 if scalar_operand: 

2282 if b0.device != dev: 

2283 return None 

2284 else: 

2285 b_zero_dim = b0.dim() == 0 

2286 for t in other: 

2287 if t.dtype is not dt_b or t.device != dev: 

2288 return None 

2289 if need_promotion and (t.dim() == 0) != b_zero_dim: 

2290 return None 

2291 

2292 if allowed_dtypes is not None and dt_a not in allowed_dtypes: 

2293 check_dtype_supported(dt_a, allowed_dtypes, dtype_error, dtype_error_type) 

2294 if out_dtypes is not None: 

2295 out_dtype = out_dtypes[0] 

2296 for dt in out_dtypes: 

2297 if dt is not out_dtype: 

2298 return None 

2299 elif dt_a is dt_b: 

2300 out_dtype = dt_a 

2301 else: 

2302 out_dtype = _promote_dtypes(a0, b0) 

2303 if out_dtype_fn is not None: 

2304 out_dtype = out_dtype_fn(out_dtype) 

2305 

2306 conts = list(map(_IS_CONTIGUOUS, self)) 

2307 if all(conts): 

2308 srcs_a = self 

2309 else: 

2310 srcs_a = [t if c else _dense(t) for t, c in zip(self, conts)] 

2311 if scalar_operand: 

2312 srcs_b = other 

2313 else: 

2314 bconts = list(map(_IS_CONTIGUOUS, other)) 

2315 srcs_b = ( 

2316 other 

2317 if all(bconts) 

2318 else [t if c else _dense(t) for t, c in zip(other, bconts)] 

2319 ) 

2320 

2321 if inplace: 

2322 # No allocation: the destination is the source, and a source that had 

2323 # to be staged is written back once the kernel has filled it. 

2324 if out_dtype != dt_a: 

2325 raise RuntimeError( 

2326 f"result type {str(out_dtype).replace('torch.', '').capitalize()}" 

2327 " can't be cast to the desired output type " 

2328 f"{str(dt_a).replace('torch.', '').capitalize()}" 

2329 ) 

2330 if srcs_a is not self: 

2331 for t, c in zip(self, conts): 

2332 if not c and has_internal_overlap(t): 

2333 raise RuntimeError( 

2334 "unsupported operation: more than one element of the " 

2335 "written-to tensor refers to a single memory location. " 

2336 "Please clone() the tensor before performing the operation." 

2337 ) 

2338 writebacks = [(t, s) for t, s in zip(self, srcs_a) if s is not t] 

2339 else: 

2340 writebacks = [] 

2341 results = list(self) 

2342 dsts = srcs_a 

2343 else: 

2344 # The one-argument form skips the keyword dispatch the explicit dtype 

2345 # form pays on every one of the sixteen allocations, and ``map`` keeps 

2346 # the per-tensor call inside the C loop: a list comprehension pays the 

2347 # ``torch.empty_like`` lookup and call setup sixteen times, which 

2348 # measured 2-3us more per call (256^2-1024^2, all three dtypes). 

2349 if out_dtype is dt_a: 

2350 results = list(map(torch.empty_like, srcs_a)) 

2351 else: 

2352 results = [torch.empty_like(t, dtype=out_dtype) for t in srcs_a] 

2353 dsts = results 

2354 writebacks = [] 

2355 

2356 _launch_binary_group( 

2357 srcs_a, srcs_b, dsts, fn, dt_a, dt_b, dev, alpha, scalar_operand 

2358 ) 

2359 _finish_inplace(results, writebacks) 

2360 return results 

2361 

2362 

2363def foreach_binary_list( 

2364 self: Sequence[torch.Tensor], 

2365 other: Sequence[torch.Tensor], 

2366 fn: Callable, 

2367 *, 

2368 inplace: bool = False, 

2369 alpha: float = 1, 

2370 allowed_dtypes: Optional[frozenset] = None, 

2371 dtype_error: Optional[str] = None, 

2372 dtype_error_type: type = RuntimeError, 

2373 out_dtype_fn: Optional[Callable[[torch.dtype], torch.dtype]] = None, 

2374 out_dtypes: Optional[Sequence[torch.dtype]] = None, 

2375 copy_semantics: bool = False, 

2376 scalar_operand: bool = False, 

2377) -> List[torch.Tensor]: 

2378 """``self[i] <op> alpha * other[i]`` for every position, one launch per group. 

2379 

2380 Both lists are paired position by position, so they must have equal length; 

2381 ATen raises rather than broadcasting across the list. 

2382 

2383 ``alpha`` scales the second operand inside the kernel. 

2384 

2385 ``copy_semantics`` replaces type promotion with assignment semantics: 

2386 ``_foreach_copy`` keeps the destination dtype and simply casts the source 

2387 into it, in both the functional and the in-place form. 

2388 

2389 ``out_dtypes`` lets the caller pin the result dtype per position. The 

2390 ``.Tensor`` overloads need it: their operand is a scalar tensor expanded to 

2391 the list's shape, and promoting against the *expanded* view would widen an 

2392 fp16 list to fp32, where ATen keeps fp16 because a zero-dimensional tensor 

2393 counts as a scalar. 

2394 

2395 ``scalar_operand`` marks the second list as one repeated single-element 

2396 tensor (the ``.Tensor`` broadcast); the kernel then reads it as a uniform 

2397 scalar instead of indexing it element by element. 

2398 """ 

2399 self = check_tensor_list(self) 

2400 other = check_tensor_list(other) 

2401 _check_same_length(self, other, "tensor list") 

2402 if out_dtypes is not None: 

2403 _check_same_length(self, out_dtypes, "output dtype list") 

2404 _STATS.reset() 

2405 

2406 # Uniform lists -- same device, dtype and (when nothing pins the output 

2407 # dtype) the same rank class -- need no bucketing at all: one launch, one 

2408 # metadata buffer. This is the optimizer hot path, so it is decided and 

2409 # executed by a helper that never touches the per-tensor bookkeeping below. 

2410 if not copy_semantics: 

2411 homogeneous = _binary_homogeneous( 

2412 self, 

2413 other, 

2414 fn, 

2415 inplace, 

2416 alpha, 

2417 allowed_dtypes, 

2418 dtype_error, 

2419 dtype_error_type, 

2420 out_dtype_fn, 

2421 out_dtypes, 

2422 scalar_operand, 

2423 ) 

2424 if homogeneous is not None: 

2425 return homogeneous 

2426 

2427 results: List[torch.Tensor] = [] 

2428 buckets: Dict[Tuple[Any, torch.dtype, torch.dtype], Tuple[List, List, List]] = {} 

2429 writebacks: List[Tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]] = [] 

2430 prev_key = None 

2431 prev_promotion = None 

2432 prev_out_dtype = None 

2433 for i, (a, b) in enumerate(zip(self, other)): 

2434 if allowed_dtypes is not None and a.dtype not in allowed_dtypes: 

2435 check_dtype_supported( 

2436 a.dtype, allowed_dtypes, dtype_error, dtype_error_type 

2437 ) 

2438 if copy_semantics: 

2439 # The destination dtype is the source of truth; the operand is cast 

2440 # into it rather than promoted against it. 

2441 out_dtype = a.dtype 

2442 elif out_dtypes is not None: 

2443 out_dtype = out_dtypes[i] 

2444 else: 

2445 # Two operands of the *same* dtype fold to that dtype whatever their 

2446 # ranks are -- the weak-scalar rule only reorders categories -- so 

2447 # the common same-dtype list skips both the probe and the four 

2448 # ``dim()`` calls that key it. 

2449 a_dtype = a.dtype 

2450 if a_dtype is b.dtype: 

2451 promotion = a_dtype 

2452 else: 

2453 promotion = (a_dtype, a.dim() == 0, b.dtype, b.dim() == 0) 

2454 if promotion != prev_promotion: 

2455 out_dtype = a_dtype if a_dtype is b.dtype else _promote_dtypes(a, b) 

2456 if out_dtype_fn is not None: 

2457 out_dtype = out_dtype_fn(out_dtype) 

2458 prev_promotion = promotion 

2459 prev_out_dtype = out_dtype 

2460 else: 

2461 out_dtype = prev_out_dtype 

2462 contiguous_a = a.is_contiguous() 

2463 src_a = a if contiguous_a else _dense(a) 

2464 src_b = b if b.is_contiguous() else _dense(b) 

2465 if inplace: 

2466 if not copy_semantics and out_dtype != a.dtype: 

2467 raise RuntimeError( 

2468 f"result type {str(out_dtype).replace('torch.', '').capitalize()}" 

2469 " can't be cast to the desired output type " 

2470 f"{str(a.dtype).replace('torch.', '').capitalize()}" 

2471 ) 

2472 if not contiguous_a and has_internal_overlap(a): 

2473 raise RuntimeError( 

2474 "unsupported operation: more than one element of the " 

2475 "written-to tensor refers to a single memory location. " 

2476 "Please clone() the tensor before performing the operation." 

2477 ) 

2478 dst = src_a 

2479 if dst is not a: 

2480 writebacks.append((a, dst)) 

2481 results.append(a) 

2482 else: 

2483 # The one-argument form skips the keyword/dtype dispatch that the 

2484 # explicit form pays on every one of the sixteen allocations. 

2485 dst = ( 

2486 torch.empty_like(src_a) 

2487 if out_dtype is src_a.dtype 

2488 else torch.empty_like(src_a, dtype=out_dtype) 

2489 ) 

2490 results.append(dst) 

2491 key = (a.device, src_a.dtype, src_b.dtype) 

2492 if key != prev_key: 

2493 bucket = buckets.get(key) 

2494 if bucket is None: 

2495 bucket = buckets[key] = ([], [], []) 

2496 prev_key = key 

2497 bucket[0].append(src_a) 

2498 bucket[1].append(src_b) 

2499 bucket[2].append(dst) 

2500 

2501 for (device, a_dt, b_dt), (a_list, b_list, d_list) in buckets.items(): 

2502 _launch_binary_group( 

2503 a_list, b_list, d_list, fn, a_dt, b_dt, device, alpha, scalar_operand 

2504 ) 

2505 

2506 _finish_inplace(results, writebacks) 

2507 return results 

2508 

2509 

2510# Every argument of ``foreach_binary_kernel`` other than the metadata pointer is 

2511# a ``tl.constexpr``, so ``(nt, fn, A_DT, B_DT, OUT_DT, ALPHA, B_SCALAR, BLOCK)`` 

2512# identifies the compiled variant and a replay only has to hand those values to 

2513# the kernel's own launcher. Triton's Python dispatch between that lookup and 

2514# the launch -- binder, cache-key hash, launch-metadata and hook checks -- 

2515# measured ~10us per call on the small shapes this executor targets, and is the 

2516# difference between the binary rows and their ATen counterparts. 

2517# 

2518# The cache is keyed on the device because a compiled kernel belongs to one 

2519# device's module, and on the metadata pointer's 16-byte alignment because that 

2520# is the only thing Triton specialises on here. ``alpha`` carries its Python 

2521# type in the key: ``1`` and ``1.0`` compare (and hash) equal but are different 

2522# specialisations of a ``constexpr``. 

2523# 

2524# Only the launcher is cached; the metadata tensor is rebuilt and uploaded on 

2525# every call, so no device-visible buffer is shared across calls. 

2526_BINARY_LAUNCH_CACHE: Dict[Tuple[Any, ...], Tuple[Any, Any, Any]] = {} 

2527_BINARY_LAUNCH_STATS: Dict[str, int] = {"replay": 0, "dispatch": 0} 

2528 

2529# One-hit memos for the two dictionary lookups that still sat on the hot path. 

2530# 

2531# ``_launch_binary_group`` derives the kernel choice, block and grid from the 

2532# metadata it just built, and ``_launch_binary_kernel`` derives the launcher 

2533# from a twelve-element key. A benchmark loop, and any caller repeating one 

2534# call shape, presents the same arguments on every iteration, so an identity 

2535# compare against the previous call's arguments answers both without hashing. 

2536# The entries hold the metadata tensor (as ``_META_CACHE`` already does), and 

2537# they are consulted only for an *identical* metadata tensor, which by 

2538# construction encodes the pointer and numel run the plan was computed from -- 

2539# a different call shape produces a different tensor object and misses. 

2540_LAST_BINARY_PLAN: List[Any] = [None] 

2541_LAST_BINARY_REPLAY: List[Any] = [None] 

2542 

2543 

2544def _launch_binary_kernel( 

2545 meta: torch.Tensor, 

2546 grid: Tuple[int, int], 

2547 nt: int, 

2548 fn: Callable, 

2549 a_dt: Any, 

2550 b_dt: Any, 

2551 out_dt: Any, 

2552 alpha: float, 

2553 b_scalar: bool, 

2554 block: int, 

2555 kernel: Callable = foreach_binary_kernel, 

2556) -> None: 

2557 # A repeated call shape reaches here with the same arguments every time. 

2558 # The twelve-element key tuple and the dict hash for it measured 1.2us at 

2559 # sixteen positions; the identity compare below answers the same question 

2560 # and the closure it calls has already captured everything but the stream, 

2561 # which is still read per call so a launch issued under a different 

2562 # ``torch.cuda.stream`` lands on the stream current at launch time. 

2563 last = _LAST_BINARY_REPLAY[0] 

2564 if ( 

2565 last is not None 

2566 and last[0] is meta 

2567 and last[1] is kernel 

2568 and last[2] == nt 

2569 and last[3] is fn 

2570 and last[4] is a_dt 

2571 and last[5] is b_dt 

2572 and last[6] is out_dt 

2573 and last[7] is alpha 

2574 and last[8] is b_scalar 

2575 and last[9] == block 

2576 and last[10] == grid 

2577 and _hooks_absent() 

2578 ): 

2579 try: 

2580 last[11]() 

2581 except Exception: 

2582 # A memoised launcher can go stale if Triton invalidates the 

2583 # compiled entry it captured. Forget it and take the same path a 

2584 # first call takes rather than raising out of the op. 

2585 _LAST_BINARY_REPLAY[0] = None 

2586 else: 

2587 _BINARY_LAUNCH_STATS["replay"] += 1 

2588 return 

2589 key = ( 

2590 kernel, 

2591 meta.device, 

2592 nt, 

2593 fn, 

2594 a_dt, 

2595 b_dt, 

2596 out_dt, 

2597 alpha, 

2598 type(alpha), 

2599 b_scalar, 

2600 block, 

2601 not (meta.data_ptr() & 15), 

2602 ) 

2603 entry = _BINARY_LAUNCH_CACHE.get(key) 

2604 # ``launch_enter_hook`` is a ``HookChain`` in triton 3.6, never ``None``; 

2605 # ``.calls`` is the list of registered callbacks, so an empty list is the 

2606 # real "no hooks" state. Proton and other instrumentation add to it, and a 

2607 # replay would then skip their notifications. 

2608 if entry is not None and _hooks_absent(): 

2609 launch = entry[0] 

2610 packed = entry[1] 

2611 pmeta = entry[2] 

2612 g0, g1 = grid 

2613 idx = meta.device.index 

2614 

2615 def replay(): 

2616 launch( 

2617 g0, 

2618 g1, 

2619 1, 

2620 _triton_driver.active.get_current_stream(idx), 

2621 packed, 

2622 pmeta, 

2623 None, 

2624 None, 

2625 None, 

2626 meta, 

2627 fn, 

2628 nt, 

2629 a_dt, 

2630 b_dt, 

2631 out_dt, 

2632 alpha, 

2633 b_scalar, 

2634 block, 

2635 ) 

2636 

2637 try: 

2638 replay() 

2639 except Exception: 

2640 # A launcher that cannot be replayed this way is not a correctness 

2641 # problem: forget the entry and let Triton dispatch as usual. 

2642 _LAST_BINARY_REPLAY[0] = None 

2643 _BINARY_LAUNCH_CACHE.pop(key, None) 

2644 else: 

2645 _LAST_BINARY_REPLAY[0] = ( 

2646 meta, 

2647 kernel, 

2648 nt, 

2649 fn, 

2650 a_dt, 

2651 b_dt, 

2652 out_dt, 

2653 alpha, 

2654 b_scalar, 

2655 block, 

2656 grid, 

2657 replay, 

2658 ) 

2659 _BINARY_LAUNCH_STATS["replay"] += 1 

2660 return 

2661 _BINARY_LAUNCH_STATS["dispatch"] += 1 

2662 compiled = kernel[grid](meta, fn, nt, a_dt, b_dt, out_dt, alpha, b_scalar, block) 

2663 if compiled is not None: 

2664 # A dispatch may have replaced the compiled entry, so the closure built 

2665 # from the previous one is no longer known to be current. 

2666 _LAST_BINARY_REPLAY[0] = None 

2667 _BINARY_LAUNCH_CACHE[key] = ( 

2668 compiled.run, 

2669 compiled.function, 

2670 compiled.packed_metadata, 

2671 ) 

2672 

2673 

2674# ``_pick_block`` searches five block sizes, and the second grid dimension is a 

2675# ``cdiv`` of the same two numbers, so ``(len(numels), max(numels))`` fully 

2676# determines both. On the shapes this executor targets the search plus the 

2677# ``cdiv`` measured 1.3us against ~0.1 for the dict hit, and the pair repeats 

2678# from call to call. The bound exists because a workload whose shapes keep 

2679# moving would otherwise accumulate one entry per shape; insertion order is the 

2680# eviction order, as in the metadata memo. 

2681_GRID_CACHE: Dict[Tuple[int, int], Tuple[int, Tuple[int, int]]] = {} 

2682_GRID_CACHE_LIMIT = 64 

2683 

2684 

2685def _launch_binary_group( 

2686 a_list: List[torch.Tensor], 

2687 b_list: List[torch.Tensor], 

2688 d_list: List[torch.Tensor], 

2689 fn: Callable, 

2690 a_dt: torch.dtype, 

2691 b_dt: torch.dtype, 

2692 device: Any, 

2693 alpha: float = 1, 

2694 b_scalar: bool = False, 

2695) -> None: 

2696 # One loop over ``a_list`` reads both numbers the launch needs. Three 

2697 # list comprehensions over the same sixteen tensors measured 3.7us; the 

2698 # loop with two bound ``append`` methods measured 2.7us, and ``max`` over 

2699 # the finished list is a C-level reduction. 

2700 ptrs_a = [] 

2701 numels = [] 

2702 add_ptr = ptrs_a.append 

2703 add_numel = numels.append 

2704 for t in a_list: 

2705 add_ptr(t.data_ptr()) 

2706 add_numel(t.numel()) 

2707 max_numel = max(numels) 

2708 if max_numel == 0: 

2709 return 

2710 nt = len(a_list) 

2711 # One flat Python list -> one tensor -> one H2D transfer, the same staging 

2712 # as ``_launch_group``. The four segments are appended into that list 

2713 # directly instead of being built as four lists and concatenated: the 

2714 # concatenation walked every integer a second time and allocated three 

2715 # intermediate lists, which at sixteen positions was measurable here. An 

2716 # in-place call writes back into its inputs, so the destination run repeats 

2717 # the pointers read above instead of reading them again. The broadcast 

2718 # operand is one repeated single-element tensor, and the kernel only ever 

2719 # dereferences its first entry, so its run is one read. 

2720 inplace = d_list is a_list 

2721 values = ptrs_a[:] if inplace else ptrs_a 

2722 if b_scalar: 

2723 values.extend([b_list[0].data_ptr()] * nt) 

2724 else: 

2725 values.extend(map(_DATA_PTR, b_list)) 

2726 values.extend(ptrs_a if inplace else map(_DATA_PTR, d_list)) 

2727 values.extend(numels) 

2728 meta = _device_meta(values, device) 

2729 # The kernel choice, block and grid are functions of the metadata run just 

2730 # built plus the three dtypes and the pack threshold, so an identical 

2731 # metadata tensor answers the previous call's answer. 

2732 d_dt = d_list[0].dtype 

2733 plan = _LAST_BINARY_PLAN[0] 

2734 if ( 

2735 plan is not None 

2736 and plan[0] is meta 

2737 and plan[1] is a_dt 

2738 and plan[2] is b_dt 

2739 and plan[3] is d_dt 

2740 and plan[4] is inplace 

2741 and plan[5] == nt 

2742 ): 

2743 kernel, block, grid = plan[6], plan[7], plan[8] 

2744 else: 

2745 cached_grid = _GRID_CACHE.get((nt, max_numel)) 

2746 if cached_grid is None: 

2747 block = _pick_block(numels) 

2748 cached_grid = (block, (nt, triton.cdiv(max_numel, block))) 

2749 if len(_GRID_CACHE) >= _GRID_CACHE_LIMIT: 

2750 _GRID_CACHE.pop(next(iter(_GRID_CACHE))) 

2751 _GRID_CACHE[(nt, max_numel)] = cached_grid 

2752 block, grid = cached_grid 

2753 kernel = ( 

2754 foreach_binary_kernel_p4 

2755 if _pack_ok( 

2756 (a_dt, b_dt, d_dt), 

2757 max_numel, 

2758 values, 

2759 _PACK_MIN_ELEMS_BINARY_INPLACE if inplace else _PACK_MIN_ELEMS, 

2760 ) 

2761 else foreach_binary_kernel 

2762 ) 

2763 _LAST_BINARY_PLAN[0] = ( 

2764 meta, 

2765 a_dt, 

2766 b_dt, 

2767 d_dt, 

2768 inplace, 

2769 nt, 

2770 kernel, 

2771 block, 

2772 grid, 

2773 ) 

2774 _launch_binary_kernel( 

2775 meta, 

2776 grid, 

2777 nt, 

2778 fn, 

2779 tl_dtype(a_dt), 

2780 tl_dtype(b_dt), 

2781 tl_dtype(d_dt), 

2782 alpha, 

2783 b_scalar, 

2784 block, 

2785 kernel, 

2786 ) 

2787 _STATS.executor_launches += 1 

2788 _STATS.groups += 1 

2789 

2790 

2791def _binary_scalar_homogeneous( 

2792 self: List[torch.Tensor], 

2793 values: List[Any], 

2794 vclass: Optional[type], 

2795 common: Optional[float], 

2796 fn: Callable, 

2797 inplace: bool, 

2798 alpha: float, 

2799 allowed_dtypes: Optional[frozenset], 

2800 dtype_error: Optional[str], 

2801 dtype_error_type: type, 

2802 out_dtype_fn: Optional[Callable[[torch.dtype], torch.dtype]], 

2803) -> Optional[List[torch.Tensor]]: 

2804 """Execute a uniform scalar list in one bucket, or return ``None``. 

2805 

2806 The counterpart of ``_binary_homogeneous`` for the ``.Scalar`` / 

2807 ``.ScalarList`` forms. ``None`` means the caller's per-tensor bucket loop 

2808 has to run: the lists are heterogeneous in device or dtype, or the values 

2809 do not all promote the same way. 

2810 """ 

2811 a0 = self[0] 

2812 dev = a0.device 

2813 dt = a0.dtype 

2814 # Uniformity and contiguity are the same walk over the list, so they share 

2815 # one pass: ``is_contiguous`` has no side effect, and the partial answer is 

2816 # simply dropped when the early exit is taken. 

2817 # ``t.device`` builds a device object per tensor just to compare it; the 

2818 # integer index is the same test and skips the construction. It is only 

2819 # available once the device has an index, which on a CUDA-only build it 

2820 # always has, so the device-object comparison stays as the fallback. 

2821 didx = dev.index 

2822 conts = [] 

2823 append = conts.append 

2824 if didx is not None: 

2825 for t in self: 

2826 if t.dtype is not dt or t.get_device() != didx: 

2827 return None 

2828 append(t.is_contiguous()) 

2829 else: 

2830 for t in self: 

2831 if t.dtype is not dt or t.device != dev: 

2832 return None 

2833 append(t.is_contiguous()) 

2834 # ``_promote_with_scalar`` memoises on ``(dtype, type(value), zero-dim)``, 

2835 # so with one dtype the whole list promotes alike as soon as every entry 

2836 # has the same class. The broadcast forms already repeat one object, so 

2837 # only a real list needs to be looked at; a plain ``float`` -- the usual 

2838 # case -- needs no tuple build and no ``isinstance`` per entry. 

2839 v0 = values[0] 

2840 if vclass is None: 

2841 if type(v0) is float: 

2842 for v in values: 

2843 if type(v) is not float: 

2844 return None 

2845 else: 

2846 v_key = (type(v0), isinstance(v0, torch.Tensor) and v0.dim() == 0) 

2847 for v in values: 

2848 if (type(v), isinstance(v, torch.Tensor) and v.dim() == 0) != v_key: 

2849 return None 

2850 

2851 if allowed_dtypes is not None and dt not in allowed_dtypes: 

2852 check_dtype_supported(dt, allowed_dtypes, dtype_error, dtype_error_type) 

2853 out_dtype = _promote_with_scalar(dt, v0) 

2854 if out_dtype_fn is not None: 

2855 out_dtype = out_dtype_fn(out_dtype) 

2856 

2857 if all(conts): 

2858 srcs = self 

2859 else: 

2860 srcs = [t if c else _dense(t) for t, c in zip(self, conts)] 

2861 

2862 if inplace: 

2863 # No allocation: the destination is the source, and a source that had 

2864 # to be staged is written back once the kernel has filled it. 

2865 if out_dtype != dt: 

2866 raise RuntimeError( 

2867 f"result type {str(out_dtype).replace('torch.', '').capitalize()}" 

2868 " can't be cast to the desired output type " 

2869 f"{str(dt).replace('torch.', '').capitalize()}" 

2870 ) 

2871 if srcs is not self: 

2872 for t, c in zip(self, conts): 

2873 if not c and has_internal_overlap(t): 

2874 raise RuntimeError( 

2875 "unsupported operation: more than one element of the " 

2876 "written-to tensor refers to a single memory location. " 

2877 "Please clone() the tensor before performing the operation." 

2878 ) 

2879 writebacks = [(t, s) for t, s in zip(self, srcs) if s is not t] 

2880 else: 

2881 writebacks = [] 

2882 results = list(self) 

2883 dsts = srcs 

2884 else: 

2885 # See ``_binary_homogeneous``: ``map`` keeps the sixteen allocations 

2886 # inside the C loop instead of paying the lookup and call setup sixteen 

2887 # times. 

2888 if out_dtype is dt: 

2889 results = list(map(torch.empty_like, srcs)) 

2890 else: 

2891 results = [torch.empty_like(t, dtype=out_dtype) for t in srcs] 

2892 dsts = results 

2893 writebacks = [] 

2894 

2895 _launch_scalar_group(srcs, dsts, values, fn, dt, out_dtype, dev, alpha, common) 

2896 _finish_inplace(results, writebacks) 

2897 return results 

2898 

2899 

2900def foreach_binary_scalar( 

2901 self: Sequence[torch.Tensor], 

2902 scalars: Any, 

2903 fn: Callable, 

2904 *, 

2905 inplace: bool = False, 

2906 alpha: float = 1, 

2907 allowed_dtypes: Optional[frozenset] = None, 

2908 dtype_error: Optional[str] = None, 

2909 dtype_error_type: type = RuntimeError, 

2910 out_dtype_fn: Optional[Callable[[torch.dtype], torch.dtype]] = None, 

2911) -> List[torch.Tensor]: 

2912 """``self[i] <op> alpha * scalar`` -- serves the ``.Scalar`` / ``.ScalarList`` forms. 

2913 

2914 ``scalars`` is either one number (broadcast to every tensor) or a sequence 

2915 of one number per tensor. ``alpha`` scales the scalar inside the kernel. 

2916 """ 

2917 self = check_tensor_list(self) 

2918 values, common, vclass = _resolve_scalars(self, scalars) 

2919 _STATS.reset() 

2920 

2921 homogeneous = _binary_scalar_homogeneous( 

2922 self, 

2923 values, 

2924 vclass, 

2925 common, 

2926 fn, 

2927 inplace, 

2928 alpha, 

2929 allowed_dtypes, 

2930 dtype_error, 

2931 dtype_error_type, 

2932 out_dtype_fn, 

2933 ) 

2934 if homogeneous is not None: 

2935 return homogeneous 

2936 

2937 results: List[torch.Tensor] = [] 

2938 buckets: Dict[Tuple[Any, torch.dtype, torch.dtype], Tuple[List, List, List]] = {} 

2939 writebacks: List[Tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]] = [] 

2940 prev_key = None 

2941 prev_promotion = None 

2942 prev_out_dtype = None 

2943 for t, v in zip(self, values): 

2944 if allowed_dtypes is not None and t.dtype not in allowed_dtypes: 

2945 check_dtype_supported( 

2946 t.dtype, allowed_dtypes, dtype_error, dtype_error_type 

2947 ) 

2948 # ``_promote_with_scalar`` memoises on exactly this triple, so a run of 

2949 # tensors sharing it can reuse the previous answer instead of paying 

2950 # for another lookup. The broadcast form makes the value's class the 

2951 # same object for every position, so only the dtype is looked at. 

2952 promotion = ( 

2953 (t.dtype, vclass) 

2954 if vclass is not None 

2955 else ( 

2956 t.dtype, 

2957 type(v), 

2958 isinstance(v, torch.Tensor) and v.dim() == 0, 

2959 ) 

2960 ) 

2961 if promotion != prev_promotion: 

2962 out_dtype = _promote_with_scalar(t.dtype, v) 

2963 if out_dtype_fn is not None: 

2964 out_dtype = out_dtype_fn(out_dtype) 

2965 prev_promotion = promotion 

2966 prev_out_dtype = out_dtype 

2967 else: 

2968 out_dtype = prev_out_dtype 

2969 contiguous = t.is_contiguous() 

2970 src = t if contiguous else _dense(t) 

2971 if inplace: 

2972 if out_dtype != t.dtype: 

2973 raise RuntimeError( 

2974 f"result type {str(out_dtype).replace('torch.', '').capitalize()}" 

2975 " can't be cast to the desired output type " 

2976 f"{str(t.dtype).replace('torch.', '').capitalize()}" 

2977 ) 

2978 if not contiguous and has_internal_overlap(t): 

2979 raise RuntimeError( 

2980 "unsupported operation: more than one element of the " 

2981 "written-to tensor refers to a single memory location. " 

2982 "Please clone() the tensor before performing the operation." 

2983 ) 

2984 dst = src 

2985 if dst is not t: 

2986 writebacks.append((t, dst)) 

2987 results.append(t) 

2988 else: 

2989 # Same one-argument shortcut as the list path: the explicit dtype 

2990 # form pays for keyword parsing on each of the sixteen allocations. 

2991 dst = ( 

2992 torch.empty_like(src) 

2993 if out_dtype is src.dtype 

2994 else torch.empty_like(src, dtype=out_dtype) 

2995 ) 

2996 results.append(dst) 

2997 key = (t.device, src.dtype, out_dtype) 

2998 if key != prev_key: 

2999 bucket = buckets.get(key) 

3000 if bucket is None: 

3001 bucket = buckets[key] = ([], [], []) 

3002 prev_key = key 

3003 bucket[0].append(src) 

3004 bucket[1].append(dst) 

3005 bucket[2].append(v) 

3006 

3007 for (device, in_dt, out_dt), (srcs, dsts, vals) in buckets.items(): 

3008 _launch_scalar_group(srcs, dsts, vals, fn, in_dt, out_dt, device, alpha, common) 

3009 

3010 _finish_inplace(results, writebacks) 

3011 return results 

3012 

3013 

3014# The scalar kernel's launcher is cached exactly like the binary one's: same 

3015# key shape, same hook check, same fail-open behaviour. The two pointer runs 

3016# (metadata and the per-tensor value buffer) both have to keep their alignment, 

3017# because that is what Triton specialises each one on. 

3018_SCALAR_LAUNCH_CACHE: Dict[Tuple[Any, ...], Tuple[Any, Any, Any]] = {} 

3019_SCALAR_LAUNCH_STATS: Dict[str, int] = {"replay": 0, "dispatch": 0} 

3020 

3021 

3022def _launch_scalar_kernel( 

3023 meta: torch.Tensor, 

3024 scalar_buf: torch.Tensor, 

3025 scalar_value: float, 

3026 grid: Tuple[int, int], 

3027 nt: int, 

3028 fn: Callable, 

3029 a_dt: Any, 

3030 out_dt: Any, 

3031 s_dt: Any, 

3032 alpha: float, 

3033 by_value: bool, 

3034 block: int, 

3035 kernel: Callable = foreach_binary_scalar_kernel, 

3036) -> None: 

3037 key = ( 

3038 kernel, 

3039 meta.device, 

3040 nt, 

3041 fn, 

3042 a_dt, 

3043 out_dt, 

3044 s_dt, 

3045 alpha, 

3046 type(alpha), 

3047 by_value, 

3048 block, 

3049 not (meta.data_ptr() & 15), 

3050 not (scalar_buf.data_ptr() & 15), 

3051 ) 

3052 entry = _SCALAR_LAUNCH_CACHE.get(key) 

3053 if entry is not None and _hooks_absent(): 

3054 try: 

3055 entry[0]( 

3056 grid[0], 

3057 grid[1], 

3058 1, 

3059 _triton_driver.active.get_current_stream(meta.device.index), 

3060 entry[1], 

3061 entry[2], 

3062 None, 

3063 None, 

3064 None, 

3065 meta, 

3066 scalar_buf, 

3067 scalar_value, 

3068 fn, 

3069 nt, 

3070 a_dt, 

3071 out_dt, 

3072 s_dt, 

3073 alpha, 

3074 by_value, 

3075 block, 

3076 ) 

3077 _SCALAR_LAUNCH_STATS["replay"] += 1 

3078 return 

3079 except Exception: 

3080 _SCALAR_LAUNCH_CACHE.pop(key, None) 

3081 _SCALAR_LAUNCH_STATS["dispatch"] += 1 

3082 compiled = kernel[grid]( 

3083 meta, 

3084 scalar_buf, 

3085 scalar_value, 

3086 fn, 

3087 nt, 

3088 a_dt, 

3089 out_dt, 

3090 s_dt, 

3091 alpha, 

3092 by_value, 

3093 block, 

3094 ) 

3095 if compiled is not None: 

3096 _SCALAR_LAUNCH_CACHE[key] = ( 

3097 compiled.run, 

3098 compiled.function, 

3099 compiled.packed_metadata, 

3100 ) 

3101 

3102 

3103def _launch_scalar_group( 

3104 srcs: List[torch.Tensor], 

3105 dsts: List[torch.Tensor], 

3106 vals: List[Any], 

3107 fn: Callable, 

3108 in_dt: torch.dtype, 

3109 out_dt: torch.dtype, 

3110 device: Any, 

3111 alpha: float = 1, 

3112 common: Optional[float] = None, 

3113) -> None: 

3114 numels = list(map(_NUMEL, srcs)) 

3115 max_numel = max(numels) 

3116 if max_numel == 0: 

3117 return 

3118 nt = len(srcs) 

3119 # The same pair that keys the binary grid memo keys this one: both paths 

3120 # derive their block from ``_pick_block(numels)`` and their second 

3121 # dimension from a ceiling division of the same two numbers, so the entry 

3122 # is interchangeable. 

3123 cached_grid = _GRID_CACHE.get((nt, max_numel)) 

3124 if cached_grid is None: 

3125 block = _pick_block(numels) 

3126 cached_grid = (block, (nt, -(-max_numel // block))) 

3127 if len(_GRID_CACHE) >= _GRID_CACHE_LIMIT: 

3128 _GRID_CACHE.pop(next(iter(_GRID_CACHE))) 

3129 _GRID_CACHE[(nt, max_numel)] = cached_grid 

3130 block, grid = cached_grid 

3131 # An in-place call writes back into its inputs, so the destination run 

3132 # repeats the pointer run already read above instead of reading it again. 

3133 ptrs = list(map(_DATA_PTR, srcs)) 

3134 values = ptrs + (ptrs if dsts is srcs else list(map(_DATA_PTR, dsts))) + numels 

3135 meta = _device_meta(values, device) 

3136 # The scalars ride in a device array of the *output* dtype, so integer 

3137 # operators keep integer semantics instead of going through a float. 

3138 # 

3139 # The dtype is settled on the host before the transfer rather than by casting 

3140 # the device tensor afterwards: that extra ``.to(dtype)`` costs a kernel and 

3141 # an allocation, and measured 0.32ms per call -- on its own more than 

3142 # PyTorch's entire foreach call. 

3143 s_dtype = out_dt if out_dt.is_floating_point else torch.float32 

3144 # ``.Scalar`` broadcasts one value into every slot, so when the values are 

3145 # all equal there is nothing for an array to index: the value travels as a 

3146 # kernel argument instead. That drops a host->device copy and a device 

3147 # allocation (~9us) from every such call. ``common`` is already known for 

3148 # the broadcast forms; only a real list needs the equality scan. 

3149 if common is None: 

3150 common = _common_scalar(vals) 

3151 by_value = common is not None and ( 

3152 s_dtype is not torch.bfloat16 or _BF16_SCALAR_BY_VALUE 

3153 ) 

3154 if by_value: 

3155 scalar_buf = meta # unused by the kernel; keeps the pointer slot valid 

3156 scalar_value = common 

3157 else: 

3158 scalar_buf = torch.tensor([float(v) for v in vals], dtype=s_dtype).to( 

3159 device, non_blocking=True 

3160 ) 

3161 scalar_value = 0.0 

3162 kernel = ( 

3163 foreach_binary_scalar_kernel_p4 

3164 if _pack_ok((in_dt, out_dt), max_numel, values) 

3165 else foreach_binary_scalar_kernel 

3166 ) 

3167 _launch_scalar_kernel( 

3168 meta, 

3169 scalar_buf, 

3170 scalar_value, 

3171 grid, 

3172 nt, 

3173 fn, 

3174 tl_dtype(in_dt), 

3175 tl_dtype(out_dt), 

3176 tl_dtype(s_dtype), 

3177 alpha, 

3178 by_value, 

3179 block, 

3180 kernel, 

3181 ) 

3182 _STATS.executor_launches += 1 

3183 _STATS.groups += 1 

3184 

3185 

3186def foreach_ternary( 

3187 self: Sequence[torch.Tensor], 

3188 tensor1: Sequence[torch.Tensor], 

3189 tensor2: Sequence[torch.Tensor], 

3190 scalars: Any, 

3191 fn: Callable, 

3192 *, 

3193 inplace: bool = False, 

3194 allowed_dtypes: Optional[frozenset] = None, 

3195) -> List[torch.Tensor]: 

3196 """``fn(self[i], tensor1[i], tensor2[i], scalar[i])`` for every position. 

3197 

3198 Serves ``addcmul`` / ``addcdiv``, whose value argument is either one number 

3199 or one per tensor. 

3200 """ 

3201 # ``lerp``'s scalar-weight forms hand the same sequence in as the second 

3202 # and third operand; the identity is what lets the homogeneity check and 

3203 # the pointer run skip the repeated third. 

3204 same_bc = tensor1 is tensor2 

3205 self, tensor1, tensor2 = _ternary_operand_lists(self, tensor1, tensor2) 

3206 values, common, vclass = _resolve_scalars(self, scalars) 

3207 _STATS.reset() 

3208 

3209 # Homogeneous fast path: one floating dtype, one device, all dense. The 

3210 # general loop below still handles mixed dtypes (each promotion is folded 

3211 # once and reused), views (``_dense``), and disallowed dtypes (which raise 

3212 # from ``check_dtype_supported`` inside the loop). 

3213 homogeneous, operands = _ternary_homogeneous( 

3214 self, tensor1, tensor2, allowed_dtypes, same_bc 

3215 ) 

3216 if homogeneous is not None: 

3217 device = self[0].device 

3218 dsts = self if inplace else list(map(torch.empty_like, self)) 

3219 _launch_ternary_group( 

3220 self, 

3221 tensor1, 

3222 tensor2, 

3223 dsts, 

3224 values, 

3225 fn, 

3226 homogeneous, 

3227 homogeneous, 

3228 device, 

3229 common, 

3230 operands, 

3231 same_bc, 

3232 ) 

3233 return list(self) if inplace else dsts 

3234 

3235 results: List[torch.Tensor] = [] 

3236 buckets: Dict[Tuple[Any, torch.dtype, torch.dtype], Tuple[List, ...]] = {} 

3237 writebacks: List[Tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]] = [] 

3238 prev_key = None 

3239 prev_promotion = None 

3240 prev_out_dtype = None 

3241 for a, b, c, v in zip(self, tensor1, tensor2, values): 

3242 if allowed_dtypes is not None and a.dtype not in allowed_dtypes: 

3243 check_dtype_supported(a.dtype, allowed_dtypes) 

3244 # ``result_type`` pairs two tensors or a tensor and a number, so the 

3245 # three-way promotion is folded through a zero-element probe of the 

3246 # intermediate dtype rather than by chaining dtypes directly. The 

3247 # integer fallback below also looks at the value's type, so that joins 

3248 # the memo key; the tuple is the same one ``_promote_dtypes`` and 

3249 # ``_promote_with_scalar`` already key on. 

3250 # 

3251 # Three operands of the *same* dtype fold to that dtype whatever their 

3252 # ranks are, so the common case needs neither the probe nor the six 

3253 # ``dim()`` calls that key it. 

3254 if vclass is not None: 

3255 vkey = vclass 

3256 else: 

3257 vkey = type(v) 

3258 if vkey is torch.Tensor: 

3259 vkey = (torch.Tensor, v.dim() == 0) 

3260 a_dtype = a.dtype 

3261 same = a_dtype is b.dtype and a_dtype is c.dtype 

3262 if same: 

3263 promotion = (a_dtype, vkey) 

3264 else: 

3265 promotion = ( 

3266 a_dtype, 

3267 a.dim() == 0, 

3268 b.dtype, 

3269 b.dim() == 0, 

3270 c.dtype, 

3271 c.dim() == 0, 

3272 vkey, 

3273 ) 

3274 if promotion != prev_promotion: 

3275 out_dtype = a_dtype if same else _promote_dtypes(a, b, c) 

3276 if not out_dtype.is_floating_point and not out_dtype.is_complex: 

3277 out_dtype = _promote_with_scalar(a_dtype, v) 

3278 prev_promotion = promotion 

3279 prev_out_dtype = out_dtype 

3280 else: 

3281 out_dtype = prev_out_dtype 

3282 contiguous_a = a.is_contiguous() 

3283 src_a = a if contiguous_a else _dense(a) 

3284 src_b = b if b.is_contiguous() else _dense(b) 

3285 src_c = c if c.is_contiguous() else _dense(c) 

3286 if inplace: 

3287 if out_dtype != a.dtype: 

3288 raise RuntimeError( 

3289 f"result type {str(out_dtype).replace('torch.', '').capitalize()}" 

3290 " can't be cast to the desired output type " 

3291 f"{str(a.dtype).replace('torch.', '').capitalize()}" 

3292 ) 

3293 if not contiguous_a and has_internal_overlap(a): 

3294 raise RuntimeError( 

3295 "unsupported operation: more than one element of the " 

3296 "written-to tensor refers to a single memory location. " 

3297 "Please clone() the tensor before performing the operation." 

3298 ) 

3299 dst = src_a 

3300 if dst is not a: 

3301 writebacks.append((a, dst)) 

3302 results.append(a) 

3303 else: 

3304 # The one-argument form skips the keyword/dtype dispatch that the 

3305 # explicit form pays on every one of the sixteen allocations. 

3306 dst = ( 

3307 torch.empty_like(src_a) 

3308 if out_dtype is src_a.dtype 

3309 else torch.empty_like(src_a, dtype=out_dtype) 

3310 ) 

3311 results.append(dst) 

3312 key = (a.device, src_a.dtype, out_dtype) 

3313 if key != prev_key: 

3314 bucket = buckets.get(key) 

3315 if bucket is None: 

3316 bucket = buckets[key] = ([], [], [], [], []) 

3317 prev_key = key 

3318 bucket[0].append(src_a) 

3319 bucket[1].append(src_b) 

3320 bucket[2].append(src_c) 

3321 bucket[3].append(dst) 

3322 bucket[4].append(v) 

3323 

3324 for (device, in_dt, out_dt), (a_l, b_l, c_l, d_l, v_l) in buckets.items(): 

3325 _launch_ternary_group( 

3326 a_l, b_l, c_l, d_l, v_l, fn, in_dt, out_dt, device, common 

3327 ) 

3328 

3329 _finish_inplace(results, writebacks) 

3330 return results 

3331 

3332 

3333_TERNARY_UPLOAD_TYPES = { 

3334 torch.float32: ("f", torch.float32), 

3335 torch.float64: ("d", torch.float64), 

3336} 

3337 

3338# ``array`` has no half-precision typecode, so the value list of an fp16 call 

3339# is packed with ``struct`` instead. bfloat16 has no ``struct`` code either: 

3340# the float32 blob is rounded through the same cast the generic path used. 

3341_TERNARY_PACK_CODES = {torch.float16: "e"} 

3342 

3343 

3344def _ternary_upload(values: List[Any], dtype: torch.dtype, device: Any) -> torch.Tensor: 

3345 """Upload one scalar per tensor to ``device`` as a ``len(values)`` buffer. 

3346 

3347 ``torch.tensor(values).to(device)`` pays the Python ``Tensor.to`` / 

3348 ``copy_`` registrations on top of the transfer, and ``to`` blocks on the 

3349 stream: measured inside a full call it cost 32us of host time against 14us 

3350 for an explicit non-blocking ``aten::copy_``. Building the host side with 

3351 ``array`` / ``struct`` + ``frombuffer`` keeps it out of the dispatcher, and 

3352 redispatching ``aten::copy_`` at ``CompositeExplicitAutograd`` skips the 

3353 Python registration. The host buffer stays pageable and freshly built, so 

3354 the staging copy is ordered before the caller can reuse it. 

3355 """ 

3356 if _ATEN_COPY_REDISPATCH is None or _ATEN_COMPOSITE_KEYSET is None: 

3357 return torch.tensor([float(v) for v in values], dtype=dtype).to( 

3358 device, non_blocking=True 

3359 ) 

3360 spec = _TERNARY_UPLOAD_TYPES.get(dtype) 

3361 if spec is not None: 

3362 code, host_dtype = spec 

3363 host = torch.frombuffer( 

3364 array.array(code, [float(v) for v in values]), dtype=host_dtype 

3365 ) 

3366 elif dtype is torch.bfloat16: 

3367 host = torch.tensor(values, dtype=torch.bfloat16) 

3368 host_dtype = dtype 

3369 else: 

3370 code = _TERNARY_PACK_CODES.get(dtype) 

3371 if code is None: 

3372 return torch.tensor([float(v) for v in values], dtype=dtype).to( 

3373 device, non_blocking=True 

3374 ) 

3375 try: 

3376 host = torch.frombuffer( 

3377 struct.pack(f"<{len(values)}{code}", *values), dtype=dtype 

3378 ) 

3379 except (struct.error, TypeError): 

3380 # A non-real entry: keep the conversion error the generic path 

3381 # raised rather than ``struct.error``. 

3382 return torch.tensor([float(v) for v in values], dtype=dtype).to( 

3383 device, non_blocking=True 

3384 ) 

3385 host_dtype = dtype 

3386 out = torch.empty(len(values), dtype=host_dtype, device=device) 

3387 if out.device.type == "npu": 

3388 # Ascend NPU registers aten::_copy_from under PrivateUse1, not under 

3389 # CompositeExplicitAutograd. Redispatching at CompositeExplicitAutograd 

3390 # skips that key and raises NotImplementedError on NPU; use the regular 

3391 # copy_ path instead, which routes through the full dispatch stack. 

3392 out.copy_(host, non_blocking=True) 

3393 else: 

3394 _ATEN_COPY_REDISPATCH(_ATEN_COMPOSITE_KEYSET, out, host, True) 

3395 return out 

3396 

3397 

3398# ATen's own TensorList grouping primitive: one C++ pass over the lists, keyed 

3399# by ``(device, dtype)``. Only the *number* of groups is needed to decide 

3400# whether a call is uniform. One call over the concatenated 48 tensors 

3401# measured 4.1us against 8.3us for the per-tensor dtype/device/contiguity walk, 

3402# and this helper drops from 8.5us to 7.0us in situ (16 x 256^2, one process). 

3403# Absent on a build without it, in which case the walk below is used. 

3404try: 

3405 _GROUP_TENSORS = torch._C._group_tensors_by_device_and_dtype 

3406except AttributeError: # pragma: no cover - very old builds 

3407 _GROUP_TENSORS = None 

3408 

3409# ``is_contiguous`` is the only per-tensor predicate the grouping call cannot 

3410# answer, so it stays a ``map`` over the unbound descriptor (2.8us over 48 

3411# tensors; the bound-method lookup per tensor is what that avoids). 

3412_IS_CONTIGUOUS = torch.Tensor.is_contiguous 

3413# Same reasoning for the two scalar accessors the launch plans read per tensor: 

3414# the unbound descriptor saves a bound-method lookup on every element. 

3415_NUMEL = torch.Tensor.numel 

3416_DATA_PTR = torch.Tensor.data_ptr 

3417 

3418 

3419def _ternary_homogeneous( 

3420 a_l: Sequence[torch.Tensor], 

3421 b_l: Sequence[torch.Tensor], 

3422 c_l: Sequence[torch.Tensor], 

3423 allowed_dtypes: Optional[frozenset], 

3424 same_bc: bool = False, 

3425) -> Tuple[Optional[torch.dtype], Optional[List[torch.Tensor]]]: 

3426 """The shared dtype when every operand agrees, else ``None``. 

3427 

3428 Three operands of one floating dtype on one device, all dense, need no 

3429 promotion, no densifying and no bucketing: the whole per-tensor 

3430 bookkeeping in :func:`foreach_ternary` is then pure overhead. 

3431 

3432 Uniformity of ``(device, dtype)`` is answered in one C++ pass. The operand 

3433 lists are concatenated into a *single* nested list: the grouping key of a 

3434 tensor in the one list is that tensor's own ``(device, dtype)``, so a 

3435 single group means all of them agree on both. (With the lists passed 

3436 separately the primitive keys each index off the first list and 

3437 deliberately tolerates cross-list float/double/bfloat16 and CPU-float 

3438 operands for optimizer state tensors, which would not be uniformity here 

3439 and, for a genuinely mixed index, raises instead of returning two groups.) 

3440 Contiguity is the one thing that call does not cover and stays a ``map`` 

3441 over the unbound predicate. Both are exact: any heterogeneity the old 

3442 walk rejected still falls through to the general path. 

3443 

3444 ``same_bc`` says the caller was handed the *same* sequence as the second 

3445 and third operand, which is what ``lerp``'s scalar-weight forms do; the 

3446 third copy then repeats a third of both walks for an answer already in 

3447 hand, so only the first pair is examined. The concatenation is returned 

3448 so the launcher can read the pointer run off it instead of rebuilding it. 

3449 """ 

3450 dtype = a_l[0].dtype 

3451 if not dtype.is_floating_point: 

3452 return None, None 

3453 if allowed_dtypes is not None and dtype not in allowed_dtypes: 

3454 return None, None 

3455 if _GROUP_TENSORS is not None: 

3456 operands = a_l + b_l if same_bc else a_l + b_l + c_l 

3457 if len(_GROUP_TENSORS([operands], False)) != 1: 

3458 return None, None 

3459 if all(map(_IS_CONTIGUOUS, operands)): 

3460 return dtype, operands 

3461 return None, None 

3462 dev = a_l[0].get_device() 

3463 for a, b, c in zip(a_l, b_l, c_l): 

3464 if a.dtype is not dtype or b.dtype is not dtype or c.dtype is not dtype: 

3465 return None, None 

3466 if a.get_device() != dev or b.get_device() != dev or c.get_device() != dev: 

3467 return None, None 

3468 if not (a.is_contiguous() and b.is_contiguous() and c.is_contiguous()): 

3469 return None, None 

3470 return dtype, None 

3471 

3472 

3473_TERNARY_LAUNCH_CACHE: Dict[Tuple[Any, ...], Tuple[Any, Any, Any]] = {} 

3474 

3475# ``_pick_block`` searches five block sizes and re-takes the max of the numel 

3476# list the caller already has, yet its answer and the grid it implies depend 

3477# only on the length of the list and its largest element, and both repeat from 

3478# call to call on a fixed workload. The cache holds the pair; a hit is one 

3479# dict lookup. The bound exists because a workload whose shapes keep moving 

3480# would otherwise accumulate one entry per shape; insertion order is the 

3481# eviction order, as in the binary executor's grid memo. 

3482_TERNARY_GRID_CACHE: Dict[Tuple[int, int, bool], Tuple[int, Tuple[int, int]]] = {} 

3483_TERNARY_GRID_CACHE_LIMIT = 64 

3484 

3485# Below this element count the transposed grid costs more than it saves (the 

3486# crossed threshold was measured on the packed ternary kernel: -0.70us at 

3487# 1024^2 against +0.07us at 512^2, which is 2^18 elements per tensor). 

3488_TERNARY_SWAP_MIN_ELEMS = 1 << 20 

3489 

3490# One-entry memo in front of ``_TERNARY_LAUNCH_CACHE``. A fixed workload 

3491# reuses the same metadata tensor object (``_device_meta`` hands the cached one 

3492# back), the same function and the same constexpr set, so the ten-field key is 

3493# answered by identity instead of being built and hashed: the key holds a 

3494# tensor, a dtype and a function, and that costs ~1.0us a call against ~0.3us 

3495# for the comparisons. 

3496# 

3497# What is memoised is the *launcher entry* ``(run, function, packed_metadata)``, 

3498# never a result or a buffer. That entry is a pure function of the dict key 

3499# above, and every field of that key is covered here: ``kernel``, ``nt``, ``fn``, 

3500# the three dtypes, ``by_value`` and ``block`` are compared directly; ``grid`` 

3501# is compared as part of the same tuple; ``meta.device`` and the alignment bit 

3502# follow from ``meta is last[0]``, since a tensor's device never changes and the 

3503# bit is a property of its ``data_ptr``. ``numels`` are not keyed separately -- 

3504# they reach the kernel as data through ``meta`` and also fix ``block``/``grid``, 

3505# which are compared. The stream and ``scalar_value`` are read from the call 

3506# and never cached. So a changed operand list, list length, dtype, block or 

3507# device all miss, and an in-place mutation of the metadata tensor's contents 

3508# cannot matter: the kernel reads that same pointer at run time. 

3509# 

3510# Only the by-value form is memoised: it is the one whose ``scalar_buf`` is the 

3511# metadata tensor itself, whereas the uploaded form hands in a fresh buffer 

3512# every call and would only pay the comparisons. A miss falls through to the 

3513# dict cache, which repopulates the memo. Measured +1.6us on the 16-tensor 

3514# ternary oop .ScalarList/.Scalar rows and +1.4us in-place, no cost on the 

3515# uploaded row. 

3516_TERNARY_LAST: List[Any] = [None] * 8 

3517 

3518 

3519def _launch_ternary_kernel( 

3520 grid: Tuple[int, int], 

3521 nt: int, 

3522 meta: torch.Tensor, 

3523 scalar_buf: torch.Tensor, 

3524 scalar_value: float, 

3525 fn: Callable, 

3526 dt_in: Any, 

3527 dt_out: Any, 

3528 s_dt: Any, 

3529 by_value: bool, 

3530 block: int, 

3531 swap: bool, 

3532 kernel: Callable = foreach_ternary_kernel, 

3533) -> None: 

3534 """``foreach_ternary_kernel[grid](...)`` with a cached launcher. 

3535 

3536 Everything except the metadata pointer, the scalar buffer and the scalar 

3537 value is a ``tl.constexpr``, so the key identifies the compiled variant 

3538 exactly and a replay only hands over the runtime arguments. Same contract 

3539 as ``_launch_executor_kernel``: no device-visible buffer is cached, and a 

3540 miss, an installed launch hook, or a launcher that raises all take 

3541 Triton's normal dispatch. 

3542 """ 

3543 hooks_absent = _hooks_absent() 

3544 last = _TERNARY_LAST 

3545 key = None 

3546 if ( 

3547 by_value 

3548 and last[0] is meta 

3549 and last[1] is scalar_buf 

3550 and last[2] is fn 

3551 and last[3] is kernel 

3552 and last[4] == (grid, nt, dt_in, dt_out, s_dt, by_value, block, swap) 

3553 and hooks_absent 

3554 ): 

3555 entry = (last[5], last[6], last[7]) 

3556 else: 

3557 key = ( 

3558 kernel, 

3559 meta.device, 

3560 nt, 

3561 fn, 

3562 dt_in, 

3563 dt_out, 

3564 s_dt, 

3565 by_value, 

3566 block, 

3567 swap, 

3568 not (meta.data_ptr() & 15), 

3569 ) 

3570 entry = _TERNARY_LAUNCH_CACHE.get(key) 

3571 if entry is not None and not hooks_absent: 

3572 entry = None 

3573 if entry is not None: 

3574 try: 

3575 entry[0]( 

3576 grid[0], 

3577 grid[1], 

3578 1, 

3579 _triton_driver.active.get_current_stream(meta.device.index), 

3580 entry[1], 

3581 entry[2], 

3582 None, 

3583 None, 

3584 None, 

3585 meta, 

3586 scalar_buf, 

3587 scalar_value, 

3588 fn, 

3589 nt, 

3590 dt_in, 

3591 dt_out, 

3592 s_dt, 

3593 by_value, 

3594 block, 

3595 swap, 

3596 ) 

3597 if key is not None and by_value: 

3598 last[0] = meta 

3599 last[1] = scalar_buf 

3600 last[2] = fn 

3601 last[3] = kernel 

3602 last[4] = (grid, nt, dt_in, dt_out, s_dt, by_value, block, swap) 

3603 last[5] = entry[0] 

3604 last[6] = entry[1] 

3605 last[7] = entry[2] 

3606 return 

3607 except Exception: 

3608 last[0] = None 

3609 if key is not None: 

3610 _TERNARY_LAUNCH_CACHE.pop(key, None) 

3611 compiled = kernel[grid]( 

3612 meta, 

3613 scalar_buf, 

3614 scalar_value, 

3615 fn, 

3616 nt, 

3617 dt_in, 

3618 dt_out, 

3619 s_dt, 

3620 by_value, 

3621 block, 

3622 swap, 

3623 ) 

3624 if compiled is not None: 

3625 _TERNARY_LAUNCH_CACHE[key] = ( 

3626 compiled.run, 

3627 compiled.function, 

3628 compiled.packed_metadata, 

3629 ) 

3630 

3631 

3632def _launch_ternary_group( 

3633 a_l: List[torch.Tensor], 

3634 b_l: List[torch.Tensor], 

3635 c_l: List[torch.Tensor], 

3636 d_l: List[torch.Tensor], 

3637 v_l: List[Any], 

3638 fn: Callable, 

3639 in_dt: torch.dtype, 

3640 out_dt: torch.dtype, 

3641 device: Any, 

3642 common: Optional[float] = None, 

3643 operands: Optional[List[torch.Tensor]] = None, 

3644 same_bc: bool = False, 

3645) -> None: 

3646 numels = list(map(torch.Tensor.numel, a_l)) 

3647 max_numel = max(numels) 

3648 if max_numel == 0: 

3649 return 

3650 nt = len(a_l) 

3651 # One tuple display with star-unpacking. Four ``list``+``map`` calls and 

3652 # the concatenations between them measured 4.28us over four sixteen-tensor 

3653 # lists against 3.77us for this form, for the same pointer run. A tuple 

3654 # also spares ``_device_meta`` its own ``tuple(values)`` conversion, and 

3655 # when the caller's homogeneity check already concatenated the operands 

3656 # (``operands``) the first three runs are read off it rather than rebuilt. 

3657 ptr = torch.Tensor.data_ptr 

3658 if operands is None: 

3659 prun = (*map(ptr, a_l), *map(ptr, b_l), *map(ptr, c_l)) 

3660 elif same_bc: 

3661 prun = (*map(ptr, operands), *map(ptr, b_l)) 

3662 else: 

3663 prun = (*map(ptr, operands),) 

3664 # An in-place call writes into its inputs, so the destination run repeats 

3665 # the first pointer run instead of reading it a second time. 

3666 values = ( 

3667 (*prun, *prun[:nt], *numels) if d_l is a_l else (*prun, *map(ptr, d_l), *numels) 

3668 ) 

3669 kernel = ( 

3670 foreach_ternary_kernel_p4 

3671 if _pack_ok((in_dt, out_dt), max_numel, values) 

3672 else foreach_ternary_kernel 

3673 ) 

3674 # Transposed grid for the packed kernel at the large end; see the kernel's 

3675 # docstring for the measurement and for why the narrow path keeps the 

3676 # tensor-major order. 

3677 swap = kernel is foreach_ternary_kernel_p4 and max_numel >= _TERNARY_SWAP_MIN_ELEMS 

3678 grid_key = (nt, max_numel, swap) 

3679 cached_grid = _TERNARY_GRID_CACHE.get(grid_key) 

3680 if cached_grid is None: 

3681 block = _pick_block(numels) 

3682 # ``triton.cdiv`` is a decorated helper and is far from free at this 

3683 # size; plain ints give the same ceiling division. 

3684 tiles = -(-max_numel // block) 

3685 cached_grid = (block, (tiles, nt) if swap else (nt, tiles)) 

3686 if len(_TERNARY_GRID_CACHE) >= _TERNARY_GRID_CACHE_LIMIT: 

3687 _TERNARY_GRID_CACHE.pop(next(iter(_TERNARY_GRID_CACHE))) 

3688 _TERNARY_GRID_CACHE[grid_key] = cached_grid 

3689 block, grid = cached_grid 

3690 meta = _device_meta(values, device) 

3691 s_dtype = out_dt if out_dt.is_floating_point else torch.float32 

3692 # Same treatment as the binary scalar path: the ``.Scalar`` form supplies one 

3693 # value for the whole list, so it travels as a kernel argument instead of a 

3694 # device buffer. The ``.ScalarList`` form still needs the array. 

3695 if common is None: 

3696 common = _common_scalar(v_l) 

3697 by_value = common is not None and ( 

3698 s_dtype is not torch.bfloat16 or _BF16_SCALAR_BY_VALUE 

3699 ) 

3700 if by_value: 

3701 scalar_buf = meta # unused by the kernel; keeps the pointer slot valid 

3702 scalar_value = common 

3703 else: 

3704 scalar_buf = _ternary_upload(v_l, s_dtype, device) 

3705 scalar_value = 0.0 

3706 _launch_ternary_kernel( 

3707 grid, 

3708 nt, 

3709 meta, 

3710 scalar_buf, 

3711 scalar_value, 

3712 fn, 

3713 tl_dtype(in_dt), 

3714 tl_dtype(out_dt), 

3715 tl_dtype(s_dtype), 

3716 by_value, 

3717 block, 

3718 swap, 

3719 kernel, 

3720 ) 

3721 _STATS.executor_launches += 1 

3722 _STATS.groups += 1
